items.title: Opinion| Famine’s echo worries South Sudan as harvests collapse
items.summary: An unforgiving dry spell is spreading across South Sudan like a slow-burning fire, sucking the The post Opinion| Famine’s echo worries South Sudan as harvests collapse appeared first on Radio Tamazuj .
items.body: An unforgiving dry spell is spreading across South Sudan like a slow-burning fire, sucking the life out of once-fertile farmlands and pushing countless families to the brink. With rains failing for this season, the ground has turned rock-hard, crops have wilted beyond recovery, and the country is inching closer to what aid workers fear could become its worst hunger catastrophe in the coming months. This isn’t a far-off prophecy about climate change; it’s an instinctive, day-to-day struggle playing out in real time. South Sudan, long identified as one of the globe’s most climate-exposed nations, is now feeling the full weight of erratic weather. The current drought isn’t an isolated event. It’s piling fresh misery onto communities already fractured by years of conflict and displacement. For families who depend entirely on the land and their herds, there is no backup plan. When the seeds don’t sprout, and the cows suffer from climate change, there is simply nothing left to eat and nothing to sell at market. The blistering heat has been merciless. Fields that once swayed with tall stalks of maize and sorghum now resemble dusty plains, scattered with brittle remains that crumble at the slightest touch. In some areas, the vegetation has become so tinder-dry that farmers worry a single spark could set entire regions ablaze. If the government does not step in swiftly, many fear this environmental disaster will morph into a full-blown humanitarian nightmare. Communities that were slowly piecing their lives back together after years of instability are now watching their fragile gains slip away through dry lands. The resilience that once carried these people through conflict is wearing thin. With each passing week without rain, the margin for survival shrinks. Community members are pleading not just for sacks of grain, but early-warning networks that can help villages prepare before the next dry spell strikes. South Sudan now stands at a crossroads. Without immediate action and a serious commitment to building long-term defenses against a changing climate, the nation risks sliding into a hunger crisis that could sweep across state lines and swallow up millions of lives. The sky remains stubbornly clear, and the earth continues to bake. For the farmers of South Sudan, every day without rain is a day closer to the edge. The writer is a South Sudanese Journalist and student at the University of Juba, pursuing a Master’s Degree in International Relations. He can be reached at khamiscosmas@gmail.com . The views expressed in ‘opinion’ articles published by Radio Tamazuj are solely those of the writer. The veracity of any claims made is the responsibility of the author, not Radio Tamazuj. items.title: Oil above $100, Nigeria faces revenue windfall, fuel price risks
items.summary: By Udeme Akpan, Energy Editor Nigeria is poised for a major oil revenue boost but faces renewed pressure on fuel prices, inflation and operating costs as escalating hostilities between the United States and Iran push crude prices above $100 per barrel. Latest market data showed that the Organisation of Petroleum Exporting Countries Basket, including Nigeria’s […] The post Oil above $100, Nigeria f
items.body: By Udeme Akpan, Energy Editor Nigeria is poised for a major oil revenue boost but faces renewed pressure on fuel prices, inflation and operating costs as escalating hostilities between the United States and Iran push crude prices above $100 per barrel. Latest market data showed that the Organisation of Petroleum Exporting Countries Basket, including Nigeria’s Bonny Light climbed 8.76 per cent to $106.30 per barrel, from more than $90 per barrel on Wednesday. The rally followed a fresh escalation in the U.S.-Iran conflict, including attacks on Iranian oil tankers, heightening fears of disruptions to crude supplies, shipping routes and critical energy infrastructure in the Middle East. Revenue boost for government The immediate benefit for Nigeria is the widening gap between international oil prices and its 2026 budget benchmark of $64.85 per barrel. With major crude benchmarks above $100, Nigeria could earn substantially more from crude exports if the elevated prices persist, boosting government receipts from petroleum-sector royalties, taxes and other oil-related revenues. Stronger export earnings could also increase foreign-exchange inflows and provide additional fiscal space for infrastructure, debt obligations and other government expenditures. However, Nigeria’s ability to maximise the windfall will depend on production currently constrained by underinvestment and other factors. Naira could gain support In an interview with Vanguard, the National President of the Oil and Gas Services Providers Association of Nigeria, OGSPAN, Mazi Colman Obasi, said: “Higher oil earnings could strengthen Nigeria’s external position by increasing dollar inflows and improving foreign-exchange liquidity. “This could support the naira and ease access to dollars for businesses dependent on imports and foreign transactions. “The impact, however, will depend on actual crude production, export receipts and the amount of foreign exchange reaching the domestic market.” Fuel prices face pressure According to Obasi, “For consumers and businesses, the oil rally could bring higher energy costs. “Rising crude prices generally increase international refined-product prices, potentially putting pressure on petrol, diesel and aviation fuel if the geopolitical crisis persists. “Nigeria’s expanding domestic refining capacity offers some protection, particularly with the Dangote Petroleum Refinery increasingly supplying the local market. “Domestic refiners, however, remain exposed to higher crude feedstock costs, while their profitability will depend on movements in refined-product prices.” Inflationary risks Obasi said: “It was gathered that higher energy costs could complicate Nigeria’s battle against inflation. “Petrol directly affects transportation, while diesel is widely used by manufacturers, logistics operators, telecommunications companies and businesses relying on private power generation. “Any sustained increase in energy costs could therefore raise the cost of producing and distributing food, manufactured goods and services.” Domestic refining opportunity It was gathered that the crisis underscores the strategic importance of Nigeria’s investment in domestic refining. Higher international product prices could improve the commercial prospects of local refineries while reducing the country’s exposure to expensive imports and external supply disruptions. For the Dangote refinery and other emerging projects, the opportunity comes with a challenge: higher crude costs could squeeze margins if refined-product prices do not rise proportionately. Nigeria must maximise the windfall Oil above $100 presents Nigeria with a significant fiscal opportunity, but weak production could limit the gains. An industry leader that pleaded to be anonymous, said: “The priority should be to raise crude output, maximise export earnings and strengthen fiscal buffers, while using expanding domestic refining capacity to reduce exposure to external energy shocks. “The latest price surge therefore offers Nigeria the prospect of stronger revenues, but also tests its ability to manage the inflationary consequences of higher oil and energy costs.” The post Oil above $100, Nigeria faces revenue windfall, fuel price risks appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Troops Arrest Two Suspected Terrorist Logistics Suppliers In Yobe
items.summary: The operation was conducted on Tuesday, following credible human intelligence on the movement of logistics supplies suspected to be destined for terrorist elements. The post Troops Arrest Two Suspected Terrorist Logistics Suppliers In Yobe appeared first on Channels Television .
items.body: Troops of the Joint Task Force (North East), Operation HADIN KAI (OPHK), have arrested two suspected terrorist logistics suppliers and recovered a large quantity of motorcycle spare parts and other items allegedly intended for Boko Haram/ISWAP terrorists operating within the Yunusari-Mobbar general area. A statement by the Acting Military Information Officer, Headquarters Joint Task Force (North East) Operation HADIN KAI, Mohammed Goni in Maiduguri, noted that the operation was conducted on Tuesday, following credible human intelligence on the movement of logistics supplies suspected to be destined for terrorist elements. Acting swiftly on the intelligence, the troops of 159 Battalion under Sector 2 OPHK, in conjunction with other security elements, said they mobilised a fighting patrol and intercepted the suspected logistics consignment at Gumsa Bridge in Geidam Local Government of Yobe State. Items recovered during the operation include large quantities of motorcycle tyres, crankshafts, oil seals, traffic indicators, acceleration and clutch cables, bearings, brake components, gaskets, piston kits, chains and sprockets, speedometers, clutch plates, rocker arms, CDI units, coils, rectifiers, fuel-related components and other motorcycle spare parts. Also recovered were 145 pairs of footwear, 2 Tecno Android phones, amongst others. The suspects and recovered items have been handed over to 27 Military Intelligence Regiment for further investigation and necessary action, according to the statement. “The successful interception represents another effort by troops to disrupt terrorist logistics networks and deny them critical supplies required to sustain their activities”, the statement added. The Joint Task Force said it remains committed to dismantling terrorist support networks across the North East Theatre. Members of the public are therefore encouraged to continue providing credible and timely information to security agencies to support ongoing counter-terrorism operations. items.title: Youth leader urges peers not to support divisive leaders, politicians
items.summary: The Secretary-General of the South Sudan National Youth Union (SSNYU), Emmanuel William Atit, has urged The post Youth leader urges peers not to support divisive leaders, politicians appeared first on Radio Tamazuj .
items.body: The Secretary-General of the South Sudan National Youth Union (SSNYU), Emmanuel William Atit, has urged the youth not to support political leaders who divide the nation through tribalism, hatred, or money. He made the remarks on Tuesday during a one-day training under the theme “Enhancing Youth-Led Legislative Reform in South Sudan,” organized by Markaz Al Salam with support from the Norwegian People’s Aid (NPA). Atit said the youth make up 74 percent of the population and that with that demographic, young people could win all gubernatorial positions and half the seats in the National Assembly, among other elective positions. He emphasized that the country needs elections to correct past and present wrongs. “If you accept money for your vote, you sell your vote and lose the right to demand roads, schools, or hospitals. Listen to leaders who talk about peace, stability, and development. As youth, we need youth centres, recreational facilities, offices, vocational training centers, schools, roads, hospitals, market opportunities, and agriculture,” Atit said. “Politicians in Juba do not send their own children to the frontlines—they use us. We must say no to violence, inter-state conflict, and tribal fighting.” “Keep your guns strictly for defending the nation’s borders against foreign invasion, not against your fellow citizens,” he added. The youth leader called upon his peers to unite and avoid deliberately being fragmented. “We must stop the divisions between civil society youth, political party youth, government youth, and faith-based youth. Whether you are from SANU, civil society, or the church, we must unite to demand the 20 percent youth representation policy,” he stressed. “Let us love, protect, and build our country. European and American nations went through worse conflicts, World Wars, and destruction before they sat down to build their nations. We can do the same.” “Do not collaborate with foreign interests to destroy your home. You are blessed to have a nationality, a passport, and a homeland—love your country like you love your mother,” Atit underscored. Meanwhile, Florence Agiba, Executive Director for Markaz Al Salam, stated that the meeting aimed at helping young people plan their approach, regardless of whether elections proceed on schedule or not. “I want to take this time to thank NPA for supporting this initiative and for always standing with the young people,” she said. “I am requesting the youth not to take this very lightly, because we know the funding space right now and how difficult it is for us to get resources to sit down and make such plans.” For his part, Michael Gorjin, Project Coordinator at Norwegian People’s Aid, highlighted that the South Sudan Youth Policy affirms a 20 percent youth representation threshold across all levels of government. “We pray this election is going to be peaceful and non-violent, where citizens claim their rights without using violence, especially since we are a generation born out of war,” he said. “I encourage you to use what we call persuasion, which is a strategic, non-violent method to influence decision-makers within your party.” “You need to register with a political party. I am not asking you to choose Party A or Party B, but to influence and be part of the process, you need to be part of a party registered with the Political Parties Council,” Gorjin urged. The post Youth leader urges peers not to support divisive leaders, politicians appeared first on Radio Tamazuj .

The Service, in a separate operation around the same period, also arrested two suspected kidnappers with N34 million in cash, which the suspects allegedly admitted was ransom payment. DAILY POST learnt on Wednesday morning that, in the first incident on Sunday, September […] NIS intercepts 17 irregular mi
items.body: The Nigeria Immigration Service (NIS) has intercepted 17 irregular migrants in Adamawa State. The Service, in a separate operation around the same period, also arrested two suspected kidnappers with N34 million in cash, which the suspects allegedly admitted was ransom payment. DAILY POST learnt on Wednesday morning that, in the first incident on Sunday, September 6, 2026, operatives arrested Alhaji Jaye, 55, and Buba Bello, 34, in possession of N34 million in cash. During preliminary investigations, the duo reportedly confessed that the money was intended as ransom for the release of a captive. According to a statement from the Adamawa State Command of the NIS, the command, in a separate development, intercepted 17 undocumented migrants at a private residence in Rumde Baru, a community in Yola South Local Government Area. The statement, issued by the office of the state NIS Comptroller, Sule Jega, explained that the migrants comprised 13 Cameroonian nationals, including eight males and five females, as well as four male Chadian nationals. The command said the use of a private residence by the migrants indicated a concerning shift in their lodging pattern, as undocumented migrants were increasingly moving from hotels to private apartments. items.title: Cameroun : démission de Maurice Kamto, la classe politique s’enflamme

items.body: © DR Entre accusations de fuite, culte du chef et sacrifice pour le parti, plusieurs acteurs interviennent pour exprimer leurs positions à la suite de la démission du Pr Maurice Kamto à la présidence du Mouvement pour la renaissance du Cameroun. 24 heures après l'annonce de la démission du Pr Maurice Kamto de la tête du MRC, c'est une véritable bataille de récits qui s'est ouverte. Persécuté qui se sacrifie ou leader qui fuit la justice ? Culte du chef ou stratégie géniale ? Tour d'horizon des réactions qui secouent le Cameroun depuis la publication sa lettre de démission mardi en journée. L'attaque frontale du Pr Aimé Bonny L'ancien allié est le plus dur. Pour lui, cette démission est la conséquence logique de l'échec du 12 octobre 2025. "On vous attendait avec le peuple, derrière le candidat du peuple. Vous avez choisi de soutenir le pouvoir qui vous a tyrannisé, par votre silence. Vous seriez rentré dans l'histoire si vous aviez pris la bonne décision : soutenir le peuple." Il conclut par un "Doux repos bien mérité" qui sonne comme un enterrement politique qui contraste avec le retrait exprime par le concerné pour devenir un simple membre du parti. L'accusation de peur judiciaire de Denis Emilien Atangana Pour Denis Emilien Atangana, président du Front des démocrates camerounais, il n'y a même pas eu démission. "Maurice Kamto n'a pas démissionné. Il a eu peur de l'humiliation judiciaire. Par crainte des décisions à venir dans les procédures initiées par certains cadres du MRC, le Pape de l'incohérence a fait semblant de démissionner." Il y voit le même scénario qu'en 2011, où Kamto aurait démissionné du gouvernement juste avant d'être débarqué. Mais, une telle posture n’a pas échappé à la critique virulente. Le recadrage du "villageois" : Pr Jean Bahebeck Réponse immédiate du Pr Jean Bahebeck de l’UPC à Atangana. Surnommé "le villageois", il estime que ce type d'attaque cache un vide : "Faire carrière dans la critique des autres traduit souvent l'absence de bilan politique à défendre. La politique exige de la constance, une vision et une mémoire politique." Et d'inviter Atangana à "regarder son propre parcours, ses alliances et ses contradictions avant de juger ceux des autres." L'autocritique : Okala Ebode sur Balafon TV Ce 09 septembre dans Sacré Matin sur Balafon TV, Okala Ebode a déplacé le débat. Il ne vise pas Kamto, mais ses militants. "Ce sont les conséquences néfastes du messianisme. On ne voit jamais, chez un leader, les erreurs, les failles. Même quand il fait une erreur, on dit que c’est une stratégie. Mais ça nous a conduits où ?’’ s’interroge l’opposant à Maurice Kamto exclu du MRC. ‘’Aujourd’hui, même dans le jeu institutionnel, on n’y est pas. On se bat pour revenir. Est-ce qu’on va dire que c’est une stratégie, ça ?" se demande-t-il encore. Il lance un appel à arrêter de transformer chaque échec en "pirouette contre le régime". La défense du parti vient d’Augustin Kouepo et de Jean Bruno Tagne En substance les deux voix portent le même message : en face, le MRC assume la thèse du sacrifice. Sur Équinoxe Soir, Augustin Kouepo (MRC) explique que "rien n'obligeait le président Kamto à démissionner. Mais comme c'est sa tête qui était mise à prix, il a choisi de mettre cette tête à côté et de laisser le MRC, la renaissance et le peuple du changement aller librement aux élections législatives et municipales." Le journaliste Jean Bruno Tagne, sur Facebook le 08 septembre, renchérit : "En décidant de démissionner, Maurice Kamto a coupé l’herbe sous le pied des persécuteurs de son parti. Il redonne ainsi une chance à ses braves militants qui, depuis 2012, se battent avec détermination, courage et une fidélité rare." L'hommage de l'adversaire : Jean Jacques Mbea Enfin, la surprise vient de Info TV. Dans Le Grand Soir, l'analyste Jean Jacques Mbea, pourtant critique de Kamto pendant la présidentielle, salue le geste : "Il a essayé en 2013, 2018, 2020... Il n'a pas réussi et il se rend compte qu'il est le problème. Il pouvait s'entêter à aller au conflit, perdre la face et nuire à son parti. Mais là, il décide de quitter. Rien que pour ça, je dis que c'est un grand coup politique. C'est aussi ça la marque des grands hommes." Et maintenant ? Le Directoire du MRC a clos le débat en interne. Dans un communiqué signé Roger Justin Noah ce 08 septembre, il prend acte des démissions de Maurice Kamto et Mamadou Yacouba et convoque une Convention nationale extraordinaire le samedi 10 octobre 2026 à Yaoundé. Appel à candidatures ouvert jusqu'au 9 octobre à 10h. Objectif : trouver un nouveau leader pour ne pas rater les municipales et législatives, comme en 2020. Cet article Cameroun : démission de Maurice Kamto, la classe politique s’enflamme est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

items.title: Recent Cases of Femicide Put Adamawa Residents in Panic
items.summary: Two women were killed within a week in Girei, a rural community in Adamawa State, northeastern Nigeria. With rumours of a third incident circulating, residents, especially women, are living in fear, while community leaders raise concerns about their safety. The post Recent Cases of Femicide Put Adamawa Residents in Panic appeared first on HumAngle .
items.body: The sight of a crying girl running towards a chemist on the afternoon of Aug. 14 was the first sign that horror had struck the Unguwar Yungur, a rural community in Girei, Adamawa State, northeastern Nigeria . “She has been beheaded,” the girl screamed. Pointing towards a motel known as No Vex Hotel, she said, “It’s Aisha! I saw him slitting her throat through the window.” Mark Sunday, the chemist owner, ran towards the motel as a crowd gathered behind him. “I did not believe it because I saw [Aisha], and we even greeted each other just minutes ago. She was with one man,” he said. When Mark entered the room where Aisha and the man were together, he saw that “Aisha was lying in a pool of her blood. There was a deep cut around her neck. She was naked, and the scene suggested that the man she was with had just had intercourse with her,” he recounted. Mark covered her body with a cloth and raised the alarm. Outraged residents pursued the suspect, who had jumped the motel fence, and apprehended him moments later. He was eventually handed over to the police. The Adamawa State Police Command identified him as Ali Haruna, a 27-year-old indigene of Borno State. Daggers were reportedly recovered from his possession, and police said he confessed to smoking marijuana with the deceased before killing her. The motel owner was also taken into custody. Police investigations are still ongoing. Little is known about Aisha in Unguwar Yungur. Locals say she was a commercial sex worker and a mother to a toddler, who frequented the hotel over the past two years after a divorce left her as the child’s sole provider. “We heard that she had an altercation with her husband, so he divorced her, and she was left to fend for the baby. Some say she started this work so she could fend for herself and her son,” a resident who asked not to be named told HumAngle. Aisha’s ex-husband has since taken custody of their son. Aisha was found lying in a pool of her blood at No Vex Hotel in Girei. There was a deep cut around her neck. She was naked, and the scene suggested that the man she was with had just had intercourse with her. Photo: Saduwo Banyawa/HumAngle. Mark said Aisha frequently came to his chemist to withdraw cash from his POS machine. “She was the kind of person that loved to greet people around here,” he added. Her killing highlights the trend of gender-based violence across Nigeria, where a woman or girl is killed every 49 hours. In rural Adamawa, the absence of active security patrols has left many women vulnerable to extreme violence. Document Our History (DOHS), a femicide observatory in Nigeria, reports that over 40 women and girls were killed between January and May 2026 in suspected gender related killings. Globally, UN Women says over a hundred women and girls are killed by intimate partners or family members daily, with Africa recording the highest rates. In 2024, HumAngle documented the murder of Falmata, a 17-year-old girl from Bama in Borno State who was killed by her uncle because she stood up to him during an argument. The incident was one of several that underscored the different forms of violence women and girls face in northern Nigeria, from killings within families to attacks by strangers. The recent deaths in Girei have renewed concerns among residents about the safety of women and girls in the region. Another woman was killed A week after Aisha’s death, the corpse of another woman was found in the hills in Girei. The deceased, Hyellachardati Benham, also known by the nickname Susuti, was a 33-year-old resident of Unguwar Abuja, a community in Girei. Born deaf, Susuti communicated expertly through hand signs and gestures. She had lived there with her older brother and his family for over a decade. “She was the kind of person who did not want to be discouraged if she made up her mind to do something. If she wants to fetch water, she will keep fetching it until she is done. She won’t even stop to rest or eat,” Yakubu Da’aya, her older brother, told HumAngle. Susuti usually went to the nearby hills to collect firewood alongside her sister-in-law and other community members. However, on Friday, Aug. 21, she went alone because her sister-in-law had gone to the farm with most of the women in the area. “She left around 9 a.m., and by 5 p.m., she was not back,” her brother recounted. Susuti usually went to the hills to collect firewood with her sister-in-law and other community members along this path. Photo: Saduwo Banyawa/HumAngle. As it grew dark, the family and other community members mobilised to search for Susuti, but after hours of searching, they did not find her. “My friend and I went to the Girei Police Station and filed a missing person report. After completing the documentation, they said we should wait 24 hours, and if she does not come back, then we should let them know so they can know the next action to take,” Yakubu said. By nightfall, Susuti had not returned, and her family started to panic. Her brother went back to the hill with some youths from the community and scouted the area for hours, but there was no sign of her. The search party returned home disappointed but went back the next morning. The group searched beyond the spot where the women usually collected firewood. They went deeper into the forest. There, they found her lifeless body. “We found her on Saturday [Aug. 22], but from what we saw, it was evident she was slain since Friday morning because maggots had already gathered on the injury around her neck. Her head was almost falling off her neck. It was also clear that she was raped,” her grieving brother said. Susuti’s body was recovered from the hill using a makeshift stretcher. The police were informed, and after a close examination, her brother took her to a morgue. “There were open wounds around her head, and since we found the corpse late, we could not keep her. Also, keeping her corpse in the morgue till the police investigation is over will cost a lot of money, which I do not have. So we buried her in Sangere with the permission of the police on Sunday,” Yakubu explained. While Susuti’s killers remain unknown, Yakubu suspects a group of cattle rustlers who have been lurking around the hilly area in recent times. He explained that the group began arriving in the community a few years ago and has since taken shelter in the nearby hills. “Their settlement is not up to 100 metres away from where her body was found,” Yakubu said, adding that the search party saw several animal carcasses and what appeared to be human remains, although they could not confirm whose remains they were. Although there have been no recent reports of missing persons in the communities, residents say such incidents were common decades ago. Across northern Nigeria, terrorists have historically operated from forests and ungoverned spaces within civilian communities. Danladi Usman, the community leader of Unguwar Abuja in Girei, told HumAngle that the hills might be a hotspot for criminals. He stressed that the entire community has been plagued by fear since the incidents. Women feel threatened “Women no longer go to the mountains to collect firewood, and if they have to, they will need a group of men to accompany them to and fro,” the community leader said. He also said locals would feel safer if the area, especially the hilly axis, were constantly patrolled by security operatives. “We are trying our best as a community to keep the place safe, but alone, we cannot do it. We need support from security forces,” he added. When HumAngle first contacted Suleiman Nguroje, the Adamawa State Police Command Public Relations Officer, on Sept. 1 for comments on the incidents and the alleged terror groups lurking in the area, he requested to be contacted later, as he was busy at the time. Since then, he has not responded to phone calls or messages sent to his official Facebook account as of the time of filing this report. Illustration: Akila Jibrin/HumAngle. When HumAngle visited Girei on Sept. 1, residents described a similar incident that occurred the previous weekend. A 10-year-old girl was allegedly raped and beheaded. The Adamawa State Police spokesperson did not respond to our request for comments on the issue. However, the community leader of Unguwar Abuja confirmed the incident, which he noted occurred in Sangere, a community situated about 30 minutes from Girei. Phoebe Samuel, a 27-year-old businesswoman in Girei, told HumAngle that she feels threatened. “Sincerely, as a lady and a young person, I feel threatened, and I feel unsafe, coupled with the fact that the second lady who was killed was raped and for someone like me who goes out in the morning and returns in the evening, I am really not safe,” she said. The absence of security operatives in the area has only worsened the fears. The community leader told HumAngle that residents are doing their best to secure the area by organising independent patrols, but their efforts were limited. The l

items.title: NSCDC arrests suspected vandal of critical infrastructure in Kogi
items.summary: The Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC), Kogi State Command, has arrested a suspected vandal of critical national assets and infrastructure in the state. The command’s Public Relations Officer, SC Aliyu Abdullahi, disclosed this in a statement on Wednesday. According to the statement, personnel of the Corps serving at the Isanlu Division in Yagba East […] NSCDC arrests suspected vanda
items.body: The Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC), Kogi State Command, has arrested a suspected vandal of critical national assets and infrastructure in the state. The command’s Public Relations Officer, SC Aliyu Abdullahi, disclosed this in a statement on Wednesday. According to the statement, personnel of the Corps serving at the Isanlu Division in Yagba East Local Government Area of Kogi State, in collaboration with local vigilantes, arrested one Adebayo Joshua, 35, while allegedly vandalising facilities at the Kogi State Project Cashew Aggregation Centre in Isanlu. The statement said items allegedly vandalised included electrical cables, which had already been peeled off, and an electrical control board. It added that the suspect was apprehended through the effective collaboration between NSCDC personnel and local vigilantes. “During preliminary investigation, the suspect reportedly made a confessional statement and is currently assisting the Corps with further investigation towards possible prosecution in accordance with the law,” the statement said. While parading the suspect, the Kogi State Commandant, CC Aletan Olumide Ebenezer, commended the personnel and local vigilantes for their vigilance and timely intervention. The commandant urged residents, particularly youths, to provide the Corps with credible and timely intelligence on suspicious activities within their communities. He noted that Kogi State is richly endowed with enormous mineral and agricultural resources, stressing that the abundance of these resources places a responsibility on all residents to protect the state’s assets and create an environment conducive to economic development. The commandant reiterated the directive of the Commandant General, Prof. Ahmed Abubakar Audi, that the protection of critical national assets and infrastructure within the command’s area of responsibility remained a major priority. He assured the people of Kogi State that the Corps would continue to deploy intelligence-led operations to check vandalism, theft and other forms of criminality. He further called for sustained cooperation among security agencies, traditional institutions, community leaders, vigilantes and members of the public, noting that security is a collective responsibility. NSCDC arrests suspected vandal of critical infrastructure in Kogi

items.body: Suspected gunmen on Monday killed three members of Kaduna State Vigilance Service (KADVIS). The incident occurred along the Zaria-Pambegua road in Kubau Local Government Area. KADVIS spokesman, Yunusa Shehu Ibrahim, in a statement explained that the personnel were on routine security checks on that axis in the state when the incident happened. It explained that the deceased tried to stop a red Volkswagen Golf saloon car but the driver refused, thereby prompting the personnel to pursue the vehicle to ascertain the occupants’ identity. He said, “The armed men in the process subsequently opened fire on the personnel, killing the three personnel.” Ibrahim identified the victims as Dallami Dantani, Abdullahi Hamisu and Zakariyya Musa. According to the statement, the attackers later went to the KADVIS office and opened fire, injured Hamisu and Musa before escaping towards Zaria. The Kaduna State Commander of KADVlS, Ali Audu condoled the families of the affected personnel and described their deaths as a painful loss to the service, Kaduna State and the country at large. He assured the families that their sacrifices would not be forgotten, while commending the deceased for their courage and dedication to duty. The commander explained that security personnel have heightened surveillance across Pambegua and surrounding areas in ongoing efforts to unearth the victims and apprehend the perpetrators. Gunmen kill three members of Kaduna Vigilance Service

items.title: It’s not acceptable – Tinubu’s Minister Keyamo fumes over attack on Peter Obi’s convoy in Benue
items.summary: Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo, has called for consistency and fairness in media coverage of political incidents following the disruption of the visit of the presidential candidate of the Nigerian Democratic Congress, NDC, Peter Obi, to Benue State. Keyamo, a Senior Advocate of Nigeria, made the call in a post on X […] It’s not acceptable – Tinubu’s Minister Keyamo f
items.body: Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo, has called for consistency and fairness in media coverage of political incidents following the disruption of the visit of the presidential candidate of the Nigerian Democratic Congress, NDC, Peter Obi, to Benue State. Keyamo, a Senior Advocate of Nigeria, made the call in a post on X on Wednesday while condemning the reported prevention of Obi by protesters from proceeding to the venue of his planned visit in Benue State. The minister said the incident, regardless of whether it was caused by internal disagreements within the NDC, as claimed by the Benue State Government, or allegedly sponsored by the All Progressives Congress (APC) or another rival party, should not be tolerated in a democracy. He said: “Yesterday’s report of the prevention of the Presidential candidate of the NDC, Mr. Peter Obi, by some angry protesters from proceeding to the venue of his visit in Benue State must be condemned by all men of goodwill.” Keyamo also noted allegations that Obi’s planned visit to Yelwata, where killings occurred in 2025, was politically motivated and intended to revive emotions surrounding the incident. He, however, maintained that such allegations did not justify blocking the former Anambra State governor from moving freely. “That is still not acceptable; everyone should be allowed to move about freely and play their politics without such crude interference,” he said. The minister, however, accused what he described as the “partisan section of the media” of applying different standards when reporting incidents involving candidates of the ruling APC and opposition parties. According to him, when an APC candidate is confronted or allegedly molested by an angry crowd, some media outlets often describe the incident as a “rejection” by Nigerians, whereas similar incidents involving opposition politicians are reported as attacks by “sponsored thugs” or “hoodlums”. “Many a time when an angry crowd confronts or molests an APC candidate at any level, the partisan Press shamelessly dubs or spins it as ‘rejection’ by ‘Nigerians’. When it concerns the opposition, then it is ‘attack’ by ‘sponsored thugs’ or ‘hoodlums’,” Keyamo said. He urged the media to avoid partisan reporting and apply the same standards to all political parties and candidates. “What is good for the goose is also good for the gander. The Press must extricate itself from such partisanship and be fair to all,” he said. Keyamo further criticised opposition leaders who, he alleged, openly encourage supporters to stone, beat or molest APC candidates in areas where the party is unpopular. He said political disagreements should be expressed through the ballot box rather than violence during election campaigns. “Whoever is angry at any candidate of any political party should display the anger with the ballot paper on voting day by a simple thumbprint, not by violent acts during campaigns,” he added. It’s not acceptable – Tinubu’s Minister Keyamo fumes over attack on Peter Obi’s convoy in Benue

items.title: Obi Urges Govt to Secure Communities, Return Displaced Nigerians Home
items.summary: [Vanguard] The presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, has urged the Federal Government to intensify efforts to secure communities affected by attacks and facilitate the safe, dignified return of displaced Nigerians to their ancestral homes.
items.body:
The presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, has urged the Federal Government to intensify efforts to secure communities affected by attacks and facilitate the safe, dignified return of displaced Nigerians to their ancestral homes.

Obi made the call in a statement posted on X on Wednesday after he visited an Internally Displaced Persons (IDP) camp in Mangu Local Government Area of Plateau State, following his inability to visit displaced persons in Yelwata, Benue State, on Tuesday.

Obi said he proceeded to Mangu after he and his delegation were prevented from reaching Yelwata, where they had planned to visit displaced Nigerians and families affected by recent attacks.

According to him, the situation in Mangu was "deeply disturbing," with more than 45,000 people reportedly displaced and over 20 communities allegedly sacked by terrorists.

"These are Nigerians who want nothing more than to return to their ancestral homes, rebuild their communities, cultivate their farms, and live their lives in peace and dignity," Obi said.

The former governor said he visited an IDP camp housing more than 500 displaced persons and offered support to the affected families as a gesture of solidarity.

He stressed the need for the government to do more to protect communities affected by insecurity, arguing that the displacement of any Nigerian should concern the entire country.

"As I have always maintained, as long as there is one displaced Nigerian, all Nigerians are displaced," Obi said.

He urged the government to protect the lives, safety, dignity and livelihoods of citizens regardless of their location, ethnicity, religion or political affiliation.

"Our displaced citizens must not become forgotten Nigerians," he said, stressing that the government must create the conditions for their safe return, secure their communities and support them in rebuilding their lives.

Obi said the continuing displacement of Nigerians had disrupted homes, livelihoods and the future of affected communities, adding that the situation required urgent and sustained government intervention.

He said his visit to the Plateau camp was also intended to draw attention to the plight of displaced citizens who, according to him, should not be left to fend for themselves.

"The New Nigeria we seek must be a country where every citizen can live, work, farm, raise a family and pursue their dreams in peace and security," Obi said.

items.title: Insecurity: North blamed Jonathan, pampered Buhari – Shehu Sani
items.summary: The Kaduna Central senatorial candidate of All Progressives Congress (APC), Senator Shehu Sani, has said the Northern elite and masses are living in denial over the cause of insecurity in the region, preferring to blame outsiders rather than look inwards. The post Insecurity: North blamed Jonathan, pampered Buhari – Shehu Sani appeared first on The Sun Nigeria .
items.body: The Kaduna Central senatorial candidate of All Progressives Congress (APC), Senator Shehu Sani, has said the Northern elite and masses are living in denial over the cause of insecurity in the region, preferring to blame outsiders rather than look inwards. He stated this in a Facebook post on Tuesday, after Minister of Defence, Christopher Musa’s recent criticism of former Kaduna governor, Nasir El-Rufai for allegedly instigating crisis in Southern Kaduna while in office was greeted with disapproval by many Northerners. Sani faulted Northerners for selectively blaming former President Goodluck Jonathan for insecurity while shielding and pampering former President Muhammadu Buhari, and now turning their criticism on President Bola Tinubu. “If Christopher Musa had blamed GEJ and BAT for the killings, he would have been applauded. It’s said that Musa failed as a Defense chief, but all those revered as opposition messiahs were also once in office like Musa,” Sani said. The former Kaduna Central senator argued that banditry originated in the North through criminal gangs and later spread across the country. He added that Boko Haram terrorism also began in the North, extended to other parts of Nigeria, and affected neighbouring countries. “The bandits and terrorists, many of whom are from our part of the country, have shed the blood of innocent people; they abducted children, raped women, extorted ransom, displaced millions and burned down the villages of our people. “The orphans and widows generated by banditry and terrorism are now IDPs in our cities and refugees in our neighbouring countries,” he stated. Sani noted that Chad, Cameroon and Niger continue to grapple with the insecurity that started from Northern Nigeria. He maintained that Northerners blamed Jonathan, “skipped and pampered Buhari,” and are now blaming Tinubu for problems that leaders from the region failed to solve while in office. The former Kaduna Central senator said, “We are asking for a miracle and magic we failed to perform. We don’t want to even hear that at a certain point in our tragic history, all the defence and security chiefs were from our part of the country; they met us with bandits and left us with more bandits.” He argued that anger is directed at scapegoats rather than at bandits, terrorists, or Northern leaders who failed to address the crisis. Sani said communities have endured violence for nearly two decades, yet there is reluctance to hold leaders from the region accountable for complicity. Sani observed that people march over the graves of victims while protecting the image of leaders who failed them, likening the attitude to patients who reject laboratory results of their own illness. “We are patients who want our diseases to be treated and cured, but we don’t want to accept and read the lab results; we want to write our own lab reports,” he said. The post Insecurity: North blamed Jonathan, pampered Buhari – Shehu Sani appeared first on The Sun Nigeria .

items.title: Giaba Urges Religious Leaders to Fight Money Laundering, Terrorism Financing
items.summary: [Daily Trust] The Inter-Governmental Action Group Against Money Laundering in West Africa (GIABA) has called on religious leaders across the region to take a more active role in the fight against money laundering, terrorist financing, corruption, kidnapping, human trafficking and other crimes threatening West African societies.
items.body:
The Inter-Governmental Action Group Against Money Laundering in West Africa (GIABA) has called on religious leaders across the region to take a more active role in the fight against money laundering, terrorist financing, corruption, kidnapping, human trafficking and other crimes threatening West African societies.

GIABA Director General, Mam Cherno Jallow, made the call on Tuesday at the National Sensitisation Seminar on Anti-Money Laundering and Countering the Financing of Terrorism (AML/CFT) for Religious Leaders and Institutions in Banjul, The Gambia with the theme, "Promoting AML/CFT on the Altar."

Jallow said the growing incidence of illicit income-generating crimes and violent extremism made it imperative for religious leaders to use their influence to promote ethical conduct, peaceful coexistence and responsible citizenship.

He said religious leaders wield considerable influence over their congregations and communities and should therefore be at the forefront of efforts to discourage activities capable of undermining peace, security and economic development.

"In promoting peaceful coexistence, the voice of our religious leaders must be strongly heard against those ills ravaging our societies, especially violent extremism, terrorism, corruption, human trafficking, kidnapping and other predicate offences," Jallow said.

He stressed that religious leaders must go beyond preaching against wrongdoing by demonstrating the values they seek to promote through their own conduct and lifestyles.

"They must not only be heard, but must be seen to lead the way by actions and exemplary lifestyles," he added.

The GIABA chief said the organisation considered the engagement with religious leaders particularly important because of the growing threats posed by money laundering and terrorist financing across West Africa.

According to him, crimes such as corruption, kidnapping, human and drug trafficking generate illicit proceeds that can subsequently be laundered through legitimate financial and economic channels.

He said the region was also facing serious challenges associated with violent extremism, making stronger cooperation among governments, institutions and influential community leaders necessary.

Jallow explained that GIABA, a specialised institution of the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS) and a Financial Action Task Force-style regional body for West Africa, was established in 2000 to protect member states' economies from the laundering of proceeds of crime and to combat terrorist financing.

He said GIABA works with member states to promote compliance with international AML/CFT standards, including the FATF 40 Recommendations, while also conducting mutual evaluations to assess the effectiveness of countries' systems for tackling financial crimes.

Jallow said GIABA had progressively expanded its sensitisation efforts to non-state actors, including religious leaders, recognising their ability to influence attitudes and behaviour at the grassroots.

He recalled that GIABA first engaged religious communities through programmes including its participation in the 2011 Annual Convention of the Ahmadiyya Muslim Youth Organisation in Nigeria, where it sensitised youths on money laundering and terrorist financing.

The organisation also participated in a security conference for church leaders in 2013, before establishing a targeted programme for religious leaders and institutions in 2017.

The Banjul seminar, he said, was the second such programme held in The Gambia, following the first edition in 2019.

Jallow urged participants to see the seminar as a call to action rather than simply another sensitisation programme.

"If we must rid our societies of these wrongdoings, then, we must continue to stand as the shining light and examples which we are; we must resist all the negative influences and help in guiding the path of our followers in building a safe and secure society," he said.

The GIABA DG, however, stressed that the responsibility for combating money laundering and terrorist financing did not rest with religious leaders alone.

The Gambia's Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU) similarly said religious institutions could potentially be exposed to abuse because of their role in receiving and managing donations and other charitable funds.

The unit urged religious organisations to maintain proper financial records, ensure transparency in the management of funds and exercise due care when receiving significant donations or entering partnerships with external organisations.

items.title: CBN strengthens supervisory focus on terrorism financing risk
items.summary: The Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) has elevated terrorism financing supervision to a current supervisory priority, as part of its ongoing commitment to protecting the [...]
items.body:
The Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) has elevated terrorism financing supervision to a current supervisory priority, as part of its ongoing commitment to protecting the Nigerian financial system from abuse by illicit actors.

According to a statement signed by Ag. Director, Corporate Communications, Sidi-Ali, Hakama (Mrs), the supervisory priority covers, at a high level, terrorism financing risk management, terrorism financing transaction monitoring, targeted financial sanctions implementation, and terrorism financing-related suspicious transaction reporting.

“The Bank will continue to apply a risk-based supervisory approach, including on-site and off-site engagement, to support effective AML/CFT/CPF controls across the financial sector in line with existing legal and regulatory obligations.

“This supervisory focus also supports Nigeria’s ongoing domestic and international cooperation on counter-terrorism financing, counter-proliferation financing, financial integrity, and the protection of the financial system.

“Further supervisory engagement will be undertaken as appropriate,” the regulator said.

items.title: Rising Tigray Tensions Test African Union
items.summary: [HRW] AU Should Act Before Conflict Escalates
items.body:
Barely a week after African leaders met in Luanda, Angola to strengthen the African Union's conflict prevention capacity, escalating tensions in northern Ethiopia are testing whether the AU can turn early warning into action .

Tensions between Ethiopia's federal government and the Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF), the Tigray region's main political party, have grown for over a year amid increasing disputes around the implementation of the AU-brokered November 2022 Pretoria Cessation of Hostilities Agreement. Both parties have accused the other of military mobilization, while unresolved questions over contested territories, the safe return of displaced people, and disarmament threaten the agreement. In August heavy fighting erupted between Ethiopian federal forces and Tigrayan forces near Ethiopia's border with Sudan with reports of artillery and drone strikes.

The AU has expressed concern about rising tensions in Tigray as far back as March 2025 and Human Rights Watch has repeatedly highlighted concerns for the safety of civilians. In April, we documented continuing abuses against Tigrayans by authorities and security forces in Western Tigray. More recently, we documented TPLF forcibly recruiting civilians in Tigray, including children as young as 15.

The political mechanisms intended to manage growing tensions are under strain. However, efforts to revive the mediation dialogue have raised concerns about whether the existing mediation channel retains both parties' confidence.

The AU Peace and Security Council, of which Ethiopia is a member, called on August 12 for strengthening the Continental Early Warning System to bridge the gap between early warning and early action. The Council validated on August 24 a new Trigger Model for Early Warning and Response , intended to connect identifiable risks with timely preventive action. Days later, at their extraordinary summit in Luanda, African leaders emphasized strengthening conflict prevention, mediation, and early warning and early action.

Developments in northern Ethiopia now present a concrete opportunity to put those commitments into practice.

The AU should intensify engagement with Ethiopia's federal government and the TPLF to address the disputes threatening the Pretoria agreement. It should assess whether the existing mediation arrangement needs strengthening and call for public reporting by its Monitoring, Verification and Compliance Mechanism on compliance with the agreement, including allegations of remobilization and abuses against civilians.

items.title: This Should Not Be Part Of Our Democracy, Keyamo Reacts To Blockade Of Obi In Benue
items.summary: Obi was in the state for his political campaign ahead of the 2027 presidential election, and to pay a visit to the Yelewata, where he was billed to meet and commiserate with victims of the June 2025 attacks. The post This Should Not Be Part Of Our Democracy, Keyamo Reacts To Blockade Of Obi In Benue appeared first on Channels Television .
items.body: Minister of Aviation and Senior Advocate of Nigeria (SAN) Festus Keyamo has joined the list of those who lend their voices against the blockade of the National Democratic Congress (NDC) Presidential candidate, Peter Obi, by angry youths in Benue State on Tuesday. Obi was in the state for his political campaign ahead of the 2027 presidential election, and to pay a visit to the Yelewata, where he was billed to meet and commiserate with victims of the June 2025 attacks. However, trouble started a few meters away from the airport when his convoy ran into a full roadblock on the two-lane Makurdi-Gboko federal highway by the angry youths. The blockade led to traffic congestion as the road was closed to all users while the police did little to disperse the youths from the highway. Reacting to the situation, the NDC presidential candidate called on young Nigerians to avoid being used as tools by the ruling class that has created the poor economic conditions they now live in. “It is ridiculous. Our experience this morning is very very worrisome. We arrived Makurdi at 9 AM, but on our way to the Yelewata community, to console and show solidarity with the family affected by the killings of over 270 persons in that community, and support them in any way I can, only to be blocked by thugs shouting, ‘Peter Obi go back!. Peter Obi go back!’ “And I was wondering: are we still in Nigeria? Because, even the campaign I have started, I should be able to move around freely. But we didn’t want to go on and cause confusion and possibly endanger the lives of other people, so I decided to remain as civil as possible. “I am using this occasion to appeal to the security agencies, the IG of police, and other agencies, to please intervene and be able to call various state governors to order. I was a state governor myself. This rascality cannot be allowed. We are a country, and can we confront these people on our own if these people cannot provide us with security? “We can not go on this way. This is unacceptable”, Obi lamented. Peter Obi addressing journalists after the blockade in Benue State on Tuesday, September 8, 2026. On his past, Keyamo noted that the prevention of Obi from proceeding to the venue of his visit should be condemned by all. “Whether the protest was as a result of internal squabbles within the NDC (as posited by the Benue State Government) or sponsored by the APC or any other rival party, this should not be part of our democracy. “Some have also accused Obi of attempting to whip up fresh emotions by attempting to visit Yelwata where the unfortunate killings happened more than a year ago just for political reasons, hence the blockade. “That is still not acceptable; everyone should be allowed to move about freely and play their politics without such crude interference. “However, there is no better time to draw attention of Nigerians and the world to the spin that the partisan section of the media usually put to such incidents. “Many a time when an angry crowd confronts or molests an APC candidate at any level, the partisan Press shamelessly dubs or spins it as ‘rejection’ by ‘Nigerians’. When it concerns the opposition, then it is ‘attack’ by ‘sponsored thugs’ or ‘hoodlums’. “Just check most headlines today. This is what is unacceptable. In fact, many opposition leaders openly boasts that the APC candidates cannot go to some parts of this country and shout ‘APC!’ without being ‘stoned’, ‘beaten’ or molested, yet the partisan Press do not call out such leaders and even help to accentuate such statements. What is good for the goose is also good for the gander. “The Press must extricate itself from such partisanship and be fair to all. Whoever is angry at any candidate of any political party should display the anger with the ballot paper on voting day by a simple thumbprint, not by violent acts during campaigns”, Keyamo stated in a tweet via his official X handle. Peter Obi’s convoy blocked by angry youths in Benue State on Tuesday, September 9, 2026. Benue State Denies Blockade The Benue State Government on Tuesday rejected allegations by Obi that thugs working for the state government blocked him from accessing Yelewata community. In a statement issued by the Governor’s Chief Press Secretary, Tersoo Kula, the state government denied any involvement in the incident and described Obi’s allegation as unfounded. The government said the claim was an attempt to drag Governor Hyacinth Alia and the Benue State Government into what it described as a possible internal political matter within the NDC. “We wish to emphatically deny that the government of Rev. Fr. Hyacinth Alia has an idea of what Mr. Obi is talking about,” Kula said. The statement also questioned whether Obi visited Makurdi on Tuesday, citing what it described as his antecedents of making untrue statements against the state. The government said Obi was not a threat to Governor Alia, adding that even if he posed any security concern, recognised security agencies, rather than thugs, would be responsible for handling such a situation. It said Governor Alia was committed to peace and the rule of law, insisting that his administration does not “engage, patronize, or deploy thugs as instruments of governance or security.” The post This Should Not Be Part Of Our Democracy, Keyamo Reacts To Blockade Of Obi In Benue appeared first on Channels Television .

items.title: CUPP chair condemns attack on Peter Obi
items.summary: Acting Chairman of the Coalition of United Political Parties (CUPP), and the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), High Chief Peter Ameh, has flayed the attack on [...]
items.body:
Acting Chairman of the Coalition of United Political Parties (CUPP), and the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), High Chief Peter Ameh, has flayed the attack on the presidential candidate of the party, Mr Peter Obi in Benue state.

In a statement on Tuesday Ameh said, “the attack on Mr. Peter Obi’s convoy, in Benue state today stands condemned. It is ridiculous and unacceptable that such action has been taken against the opposition.

“I strongly condemn the roadblock and intimidation reportedly carried out by individuals in Benue, allegedly with the backing of those in power. No citizen should be subjected to harassment, threats, or unnecessary obstruction on a public road. Our roads belong to the people, and political influence must never be used to create fear, inconvenience, or a sense of lawlessness.

“These actions violate the fundamental rights guaranteed under the 1999 Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria (as amended). Section 41(1) provides that “Every citizen of Nigeria is entitled to move freely throughout Nigeria and to reside in any part thereof…” Section 40 further guarantees that “Every person shall be entitled to assemble freely and associate with other persons, and in particular he may form or belong to any political party, trade union or any other association for the protection of his interests.”

“The Benue state government must openly condemn this incident and ensure that Mr. Peter Obi’s visit to Benue proceeds without any distractions or further interference.

“We must continue to speak up for peace, accountability, and the rule of law. Benue deserves leadership that protects its people and respect our constitutional rights, not actions that harass, intimidate, or humiliate our citizens.

“I call on the relevant authorities to investigate this incident transparently and ensure that those responsible are held accountable, regardless of their APC connections,” the CUPP leader said.

items.title: Obi’s blocked Benue visit, media bias unacceptable — Keyamo
items.summary: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA — Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo, SAN, has condemned the blockade of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) presidential candidate, Peter Obi, by protesters in Benue State, describing the incident as unacceptable in a democracy. Keyamo, who spoke with Vanguard, also accused sections of the media of applying different […] The post Obi’s blocked Be
items.body: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA — Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo, SAN, has condemned the blockade of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) presidential candidate, Peter Obi, by protesters in Benue State, describing the incident as unacceptable in a democracy. Keyamo, who spoke with Vanguard, also accused sections of the media of applying different standards in reporting similar incidents depending on the political party involved. He said the prevention of Obi from proceeding to the venue of his planned visit must be condemned, irrespective of the identity or affiliation of those responsible. “Whether the protest was as a result of internal squabbles within the NDC, as posited by the Benue State Government, or sponsored by the All Progressives Congress, APC, or any other rival party, this should not be part of our democracy,” he said. The minister acknowledged claims that Obi’s planned visit to Yelwata, a community that suffered deadly attacks, was politically motivated and that the visit had triggered opposition from some protesters. He, however, said such grievances could not justify preventing the former Anambra State governor from moving freely. “That is still not acceptable; everyone should be allowed to move about freely and play their politics without such crude interference,” Keyamo said. He said the incident should also prompt Nigerians to examine what he described as partisan coverage of political protests by sections of the media. According to him, some media outlets describe hostile crowds confronting All Progressives Congress, APC, candidates as evidence of “rejection” by Nigerians, while similar incidents involving opposition politicians are reported as attacks by “sponsored thugs” or “hoodlums”. “When it concerns the opposition, then it is ‘attack’ by ‘sponsored thugs’ or ‘hoodlums’. Just check most headlines today,” he said. Keyamo also alleged that some opposition politicians had openly threatened that APC candidates would face attacks if they visited certain parts of the country and openly identified with the party. He criticised what he described as the failure of sections of the media to adequately challenge or condemn such statements. “What is good for the goose is also good for the gander. The Press must extricate itself from such partisanship and be fair to all,” the minister said. Keyamo urged supporters of all political parties to exercise restraint during the campaign season, stressing that political disagreements should be settled through democratic processes. He said voters dissatisfied with any candidate should express their opposition through the ballot box rather than violence. “Whoever is angry at any candidate of any political party should display the anger with the ballot paper on voting day by a simple thumbprint, not by violent acts during campaigns,” Keyamo cautioned. items.title: R306 million spent on June 30 anti-immigration protests - R251 million gone just on overtime
items.summary: The South African Police Service has spent more than R306 million policing the June 30 anti-immigration protests, with overtime alone accounting for nearly R252 million.
items.body:
A tense confrontation during anti-immigration protests in Durban. The police service says it spent R306 million on the June 30 protests, with R251 million going just on overtime.

The South African Police Service (SAPS) spent R306.2 million on the June 30 deployment linked to nationwide protests against illegal immigration, with R251.8 million spent on overtime alone.

This was revealed by acting Police Minister Professor Firoz Cachalia in a parliamentary reply.

The SAPS had previously allocated R600 million for policing and security operations related to the protests against illegal immigration on June 30.

The deployment was in response to nationwide demonstrations led by the anti-migrant group March and March movement , which called on undocumented immigrants to self-deport.

The high price tag was met with mixed reactions from opposition parties, which slammed it as a waste of taxpayers’ money.

Cachalia was responding to questions posed by African Transformation Movement (ATM) leader Vuyo Zungula, who asked how much of the reported R600 million allocation had been spent on policing and security operations for the June 30 protests.

Zungula also requested a detailed breakdown of the expenditure by category, including overtime, operational costs, equipment, transport, accommodation and other goods and services. He also asked for details of service providers and suppliers, where applicable, as well as the geographic areas of deployment.

Zungula further asked which service providers, contractors and suppliers received payments in relation to the operations, how much was paid to each, what goods or services were procured and which procurement process was followed.

He also asked Cachalia how much remained unspent from the reported R600 million allocation and what specific purposes SAPS intended to use the remaining balance for.

In response, Cachalia said that, according to the latest available information, expenditure of R306,208,477 was incurred by SAPS in respect of deployments for the June 30 protests.

“This amount comprises overtime payments, subsistence and travel allowances, accommodation costs and the remuneration of reservists called up for the event.”

“Other costs not directly recorded against the project, such as fuel costs, communication expenses and additional visibility costs, are not included in the amount reflected above.”

Cachalia said officers deployed away from their normal places of work who required accommodation were responsible for arranging and paying for their own accommodation.

“The expenditure incurred was subsequently reimbursed through the applicable travel and subsistence claims process. Consequently, accommodation service providers were not paid directly by the South African Police Service through the electronic supplier payment system; instead, payment was made by the individual members concerned.”

Cachalia said the expenditure related predominantly to the remuneration of personnel, including overtime, travel and subsistence allowances and the remuneration of reservists, rather than the procurement of goods or services from external service providers.

“As indicated, accommodation costs were paid by individual members and reimbursed through the travel and subsistence claims process, rather than through direct payments to suppliers via the electronic supplier payment system.”

“Accordingly, no external service providers, contractors or suppliers received direct payments from the South African Police Service in relation to the operations for the specified event.”

He said the SAPS was still finalising outstanding claims relating to reservist remuneration, overtime payments and travel claims.

“Any remaining balance will be utilised to support preparatory and operational requirements associated with the forthcoming Local Government Elections, including expenditure on fuel and vehicle maintenance to enhance operational visibility.”

Meanwhile, the anti-migrant group has planned further protests against undocumented migration for September 30.

The movement has called for a new National Day of Action on September 30, putting authorities under renewed pressure to deploy scarce resources while managing the legal and humanitarian obligations attached to immigration enforcement.

The Inter-Ministerial Committee (IMC) on Migration has remained tight-lipped about the policing, deportation and repatriation costs for the planned September 30 protests.

During a media briefing on Tuesday, the committee said it had undertaken multidisciplinary law enforcement operations targeting illegal border crossings, fraudulent documentation, labour exploitation, human trafficking networks, illegal mining operations and other forms of organised crime linked to migration vulnerabilities.

National Joint Operational and Intelligence Structure (NATJOINTS) Chairperson Lieutenant-General Tebello Mosikili, when asked about the costs of policing the September 30 protests, said normal policing would continue.

“There will be no specific budget. We work on the budget allocated on the baseline, and we are continuing.”

“There are marches that were announced even prior to the September one; if it is pronounced that every Thursday there will be marches, we are continuing to manage and police those. Policing will continue,” Mosikili said.

items.title: Benue govt not thugs blocked Obi’s convoy – Sowore alleges
items.summary: The AAC candidate said the alleged presence of a special adviser to the Benue State governor among the crowd reinforced his belief that the action was government-sponsored. The post Benue govt not thugs blocked Obi’s convoy – Sowore alleges appeared first on Vanguard News .
items.body: The presidential candidate of the African Action Congress (AAC), Omoyele Sowore, has alleged that the Benue State Government was behind the blockade of Peter Obi’s convoy during the former Anambra State governor’s visit to the state on Tuesday. Sowore said the incident, during which a crowd reportedly prevented Obi and his delegation from proceeding and chanted for him to leave, was planned to stop him from entering Makurdi. The AAC candidate said the alleged presence of a special adviser to the Benue State governor among the crowd reinforced his belief that the action was government-sponsored. “The clearer indication that the government was involved was actually made available by Mr. Peter Obi himself, who stated clearly that one of the special advisers to the governor was seen as part of the crowd that was chanting, ‘Peter Obi, go back,’” Sowore said. “My position is that nobody should be prevented from going anywhere in Nigeria. You need not doubt that this was government-sponsored.” He alleged that the conduct of the crowd and security agencies at the scene suggested that those involved were known to the authorities. “I think the state governor or his people have responded as expected—they know who did it, and I’m sure they were part of the planning to prevent him from entering Makurdi, and that’s a shame,” he added. Despite his political differences with Obi, Sowore said his disagreements with the former presidential candidate were ideological and not personal, insisting that no Nigerian should be denied the right to move freely or campaign because of political affiliation. “I don’t want any harm to come upon him, any member of his delegation, or his campaign team wherever they go in Nigeria,” he said. Sowore also warned that the incident could signal a growing pattern of political intimidation ahead of the 2027 elections. “They are just testing the waters. If this works, then nobody is safe; you will find more of these kinds of intimidation attacks, and it will quickly snowball into assassinations,” he said. He called on Nigerians and political candidates to reject intimidation and violence, urging authorities to identify and sanction those responsible for the incident.
