items.title: SDP will eliminate poverty, end insecurity within four years — Adebayo
items.summary: The Social Democratic Party (SDP) presidential candidate, Adewole Adebayo, has promised to eliminate poverty and tackle insecurity within four years if elected president in the 2027 general election. The post SDP will eliminate poverty, end insecurity within four years — Adebayo appeared first on The Sun Nigeria .
items.body: The Social Democratic Party (SDP) presidential candidate, Adewole Adebayo, has promised to eliminate poverty and tackle insecurity within four years if elected president in the 2027 general election. Adebayo made the pledge while unveiling his presidential blueprint, Farewell to Poverty and Insecurity, in Abuja and later discussing the policy document in an interview on ARISE NEWS. He described the blueprint as a comprehensive alternative for addressing Nigeria’s economic and security challenges, insisting that its proposals were anchored on the Nigerian Constitution. “First, the most important thing about the blueprint is that it complies with the Constitution. Section 224 of the Constitution says that the manifesto or policy of every political party must comply. Only the SDP complies. So we have followed the Constitution,” he said. Adebayo expressed confidence that the policies could produce significant improvements in the country within a single presidential term. “At the end of the four-year term, we will have eliminated poverty. I’m not saying every Nigerian is going to be a billionaire, but we will eliminate poverty and deal with insecurity,” he said. According to him, the SDP’s programme is built around a clear national development philosophy rather than the pursuit of political power for its own sake. He said the party planned to release 16 additional policy books detailing solutions to various national challenges and argued that the policies should be useful beyond the SDP. “What we want to do in the SDP is use what we have that they don’t have: we have the intellect and we have the philosophy. So we will first solve the problems,” Adebayo said. He said the party’s economic strategy would focus on addressing the structural causes of poverty through education, agriculture, healthcare, housing, infrastructure and employment. Adebayo described education as the most important tool for lifting young Nigerians out of poverty and promised to ensure that every child of school age is enrolled in school. “The fastest train out of the station of poverty is education,” he said, adding that the SDP would seek to achieve universal school enrolment within three months of taking office. He also promised greater investment in agriculture to improve food production and reduce the cost of feeding Nigerians. Adebayo cited Kaduna, Nasarawa and Benue states as examples of areas with the potential to produce enough food to supply other parts of the country if properly supported. On healthcare, he said the government would expand access to medical services so that citizens would not be pushed into poverty by healthcare costs. “You are allowed to be broke without being poor, in the sense that you can afford food, you are not using more than 9% or 8% of your income for housing, and you are not paying anything for medical care because that’s your right,” he said. The SDP candidate also promised to reduce unemployment to between two and three per cent through massive infrastructure projects, agricultural investment and expansion of social services. He said such investments would create jobs for teachers, healthcare workers and other professionals while simultaneously improving public services. On electricity, Adebayo proposed decentralised solar power generation, promising to install between 11 and 15 kilowatts of solar capacity on every roof within 11 months if elected. “Just making solar panels, for example, to reduce energy failure—I promise that between 11 to 15 kilowatts of solar power will be put on every roof within 11 months,” he said. He projected that the solar clusters could generate up to 32,000 megawatts and said the national grid would function mainly as a backup to the decentralised system. Adebayo also reiterated his support for a mixed economy in which government makes strategic investments alongside the private sector, particularly in areas capable of generating employment and strengthening domestic production. On his political prospects, he expressed confidence that the SDP could win enough legislative seats to implement its proposed reforms, citing the party’s previous experience in securing Senate and House of Representatives seats. He said Nigerians would support the party once they understood its policy proposals. Adebayo further pledged that his administration would prioritise national unity over party identity if elected, saying the Nigerian flag would represent his allegiance. “My flag when I become president is green-white-green; it is not the orange of the SDP anymore,” he said. The post SDP will eliminate poverty, end insecurity within four years — Adebayo appeared first on The Sun Nigeria .

items.title: CUPP condemns attack on Obi’s convoy in Benue, warns against thuggery ahead of 2027
items.summary: The Coalition of United Political Parties (CUPP) has condemned the reported obstruction and attack on the convoy of Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) Presidential Candidate, Mr. Peter Obi, in Benue State, describing it as a manifestation of political intolerance that threatens Nigeria’s democracy. The post CUPP condemns attack on Obi’s convoy in Benue, warns against thuggery ahead of 2027 appeared
items.body: From Stanley Uzoaru, Owerri The Coalition of United Political Parties (CUPP) has condemned the reported obstruction and attack on the convoy of Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) Presidential Candidate, Mr. Peter Obi, in Benue State, describing it as a manifestation of political intolerance that threatens Nigeria’s democracy. In a statement issued Wednesday and signed by its spokesperson, Comrade Diamond Bryan Agu, CUPP said Mr. Obi’s convoy was blocked by youths on Tuesday, September 8, 2026, along the Gboko Road and the Gboko–Makurdi Expressway in Makurdi as he traveled toward Yelwata in Guma Local Government Area. Mr. Obi, a former Governor of Anambra State and the Labour Party’s 2023 presidential candidate, was in Benue in connection with activities relating to victims of the Yelwata killings. CUPP called the incident “unacceptable in a constitutional democracy” and demanded an immediate investigation. While noting that allegations of political sponsorship are still subject to investigation, the coalition said it was troubling that an opposition presidential candidate was subjected to such treatment during a lawful visit within the country. “Nigeria is not a political fiefdom. Benue State belongs to every Nigerian,” the statement read. CUPP cited Sections 39, 40 and 41 of the 1999 Constitution, which guarantee freedom of expression, peaceful assembly and association, and freedom of movement. It argued that Mr. Obi “requires neither a visa nor political permission to enter Benue State or any other state of the federation,” and that his political identity cannot lawfully be used to restrict his movement or intimidate his supporters. The coalition linked the Benue incident to what it described as a growing atmosphere of hostility toward opposition activities ahead of the 2027 general elections. It referenced a February 24, 2026 attack in Benin City, Edo State, where Mr. Obi and other opposition figures were reportedly caught up in violence following an ADC engagement. CUPP challenged the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) to prove that its commitment to democracy goes “beyond electoral rhetoric,” adding that “elections are not wars, and political opponents are not enemies of the state.” It also called on Benue State Governor, Rev. Fr. Hyacinth Alia, to “rise above partisan considerations and demonstrate the virtues of tolerance, peace and human dignity expected of a leader and Catholic priest.” “If political opponents cannot freely enter states governed by the ruling party, engage citizens and express their political views without intimidation, then Nigerians have every reason to question the quality of democracy being practised,” CUPP said. The coalition demanded that the Inspector-General of Police, the Department of State Services and other security agencies conduct what it termed a “painstaking, independent and transparent investigation” into the Benue incident, identify those responsible, and ensure prosecution. “The opposition will not be intimidated,” the statement said. “CUPP warns that Nigeria cannot afford a 2027 campaign season characterised by political thuggery, intimidation, road blockades and violence. Such conduct is barbaric, anti-democratic and fundamentally incompatible with constitutional governance.” CUPP stressed that the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory constitute one indivisible federation, and that no governor, party, or political group has the authority to determine which Nigerian may enter any part of the country. It urged Nigerians to reject political intimidation and defend constitutional freedoms. “Democracy must not be reduced to the freedom to vote on election day. It must include the freedom to campaign, organise, associate, travel and speak without fear,” the coalition concluded. items.title: Nigeria’s kidnapping map is changing as armed groups move into new territories
items.summary: Nigeria’s kidnapping crisis is entering a more difficult phase. Military operations are disrupting established criminal networks, but armed groups are read more Nigeria’s kidnapping map is changing as armed groups move into new territories
items.body: Nigeria’s kidnapping crisis is entering a more difficult phase. Military operations are disrupting established criminal networks, but armed groups are adapting by abandoning exposed hideouts, moving between local government areas and exploiting new transport corridors. The result is a more mobile security threat that is increasingly difficult to contain within state boundaries. A recent assessment by SBM Intelligence points to a shift in the geography of kidnapping. Criminal networks are not necessarily tied to the communities where they first established themselves. As security forces intensify operations, groups can move between roads, forests and settlements, creating risks in areas that previously experienced fewer attacks. Kogi offers one of the clearest examples. SBM’s analysis of the August 30 rescue of 21 kidnapped people, including 15 National Youth Service Corps members, suggests the mass abduction in Ofu was unlikely to have been carried out by the network associated with the late Kachalla Battijo. Instead, the evidence points to an independent Fulani armed gang operating along established highway corridors. That distinction matters. The death or disruption of a prominent kidnapping kingpin does not necessarily remove the geography, infrastructure or incentives that allow another group to operate in the same area. From fixed hideouts to mobile corridors SBM’s Violence Tracker recorded more than 31 people abducted in Ofu in a recurring pattern of highway kidnappings before Battijo’s death. This differed from Battijo’s reported pattern of targeting institutions, including a failed attempt to abduct students at Government Secondary School in Iluke. The latest assessment identifies the Itobe–Anyigba/Itobe–Ochadamu corridor and the Aloma–Egane–Onicha-Igo route as potential areas for further attacks. The concern is that military operations may push kidnappers from one road to another rather than remove them from the wider theatre. A group does not need to control a town or maintain a permanent camp to operate. It can move between forests and roads, exploiting gaps between security jurisdictions. Nigeria has seen similar displacement elsewhere. SBM previously reported that military pressure on bandit camps in Zamfara and Katsina was pushing displaced groups towards Kano, particularly Rogo Local Government Area. The latest assessment suggests a similar dynamic could be emerging further south. Kogi’s roads become a new front line Kogi’s position makes this particularly significant. The state connects Nigeria’s north-central and southern regions, with major roads carrying commuters, traders and other travellers across the country. Its forests and less populated areas also offer potential escape routes. As security forces concentrate on known locations, criminal networks have an incentive to seek less protected routes. This creates a cycle of catch-up: security forces clear one corridor, criminal groups shift to another, and the pattern repeats. The same flexibility is emerging around the Federal Capital Territory. SBM identified targeted abductions involving retired senior military officers and their relatives. Between March and September 2026, its Violence Tracker recorded eight people abducted and one killed in incidents involving senior military personnel or their relatives. The proximity of the incidents is significant. The report puts the furthest distance between identified abduction points at about 52km, between Karshi and ACO Estate. This suggests the possibility of a locally embedded network operating across the FCT and neighbouring parts of Nasarawa, Niger and Kaduna, rather than a gang confined to Abuja. Ghana is monetising attention but Nigeria is leaving it on the table UCL Roundup: Real Madrid win, Haaland stars for Man City, Villa stun Brugge WORLD IN BRIEF:UK sanctions West Bank settlements, Renoir paintings worth €18m stolen, Sudan health system nears collapse and other stories The implication is important: kidnapping is no longer simply a remote highway problem. Criminal networks can operate close to major population centres while using surrounding forests and boundary communities to move victims and evade security forces. Military victories can create smaller threats The north-west offers another warning. Security forces recently killed high-profile figures linked to Kachalla Filani’s network in Katsina, while Kachalla Hare was killed near Gusami in Zamfara. These operations could weaken the groups in the short term. But SBM warns that leadership losses may produce fragmentation rather than disappearance. Filani’s network could split into smaller mobile cells along the Matazu–Musawa–Dutsinma–Kankia axis, while Hare’s surviving fighters could disperse across the Mada–Gusami–Bungudu/Gusau corridor. Read also Nigerian gunmen raise over $5 million from mass kidnappings, study finds This creates a paradox. Military operations can reduce the capacity of large criminal organisations while encouraging surviving fighters to form smaller, harder-to-detect groups. Such groups may be less capable of holding territory but can remain dangerous by shifting between kidnapping, cattle rustling and other criminal activities. Nigeria may be fighting the wrong map The persistence of kidnapping is ultimately tied to its economics. Criminal groups do not need to permanently occupy territory if they can repeatedly exploit roads, forests and communities. Local intelligence, motorcycles, escape routes and knowledge of transport patterns provide much of the infrastructure they need. Geographic displacement therefore does not mean the disappearance of the business. The economic costs extend beyond victims. Dangerous roads raise risks for transport operators, increase security costs for businesses and disrupt farmers and traders. Kogi has already temporarily closed selected markets and motor parks in parts of Kogi West as security forces intensified operations. Such measures may disrupt criminal logistics, but they also restrict legitimate commerce. The central lesson from SBM’s assessment is that Nigeria’s kidnapping problem cannot be understood simply by counting attacks by state. The more important question is how criminal networks move between them. A gang operating around a forest does not recognise administrative boundaries. Yet Nigeria’s security architecture remains heavily organised around them, creating gaps mobile networks can exploit. The challenge is therefore not simply to capture more kidnappers. It is to build an intelligence system capable of tracking how criminal networks, weapons, money and personnel move across corridors. The rescue of the NYSC members shows that security forces can intervene successfully after an abduction. But rescue is not the same as dismantling the network responsible. Nigeria may continue winning individual battles against kidnapping gangs while losing ground in the wider geography of insecurity. The map is changing. The question is whether the security response can change with it. Obidike Okafor Obidike Okafor is an award winning, seasoned journalist and content consultant. Obidike has left his mark on the global stage, writing for prestigious publications in Nigeria, the UK, South Africa, Kenya, Germany, and Senegal. He also has experience as an editor, research analyst and podcaster.

items.title: Nigeria: Soldier Injured As Military Repels ISWAP Attack On Military Base
items.summary: [Premium Times] The soldier whose identity was not disclosed sustained gunshot injury to his left arm, and was being treated, according to a statement by Mohammed Goni, the spokesperson for Operation Hadin Kai, a joint task force in the North-east.
items.body:
The soldier whose identity was not disclosed sustained gunshot injury to his left arm, and was being treated, according to a statement by Mohammed Goni, the spokesperson for Operation Hadin Kai, a joint task force in the North-east.

The Nigerian military says one soldier sustained an injury during a failed Islamic State West Africa Province (ISWAP) attack on a military base in Pulka, Gwoza Local Government Area of Borno State.

The soldier whose identity was not disclosed sustained gunshot injury to his left arm, and was being treated, according to a statement by Mohammed Goni, the spokesperson for Operation Hadin Kai, a joint task force in the North-east.

Mr Goni, a Nigerian Army captain, stated that the terrorists attempted to overrun the military base on Monday, but were resisted by the ground troops, including members of Civilian Joint Task Force (CJTF).

The ground troops, he said, were assisted by the air component of operation Hadin Kai, which provided Intelligence, Surveillance and Reconnaissance (ISR) during the attack.

This coordinated response forced the terrorists to retreat "with casualties."

"As the terrorists attempted to escape following the fierce resistance from ground troops, the air component conducted precision strikes on identified hostile elements, disrupting their withdrawal and further frustrating their efforts to regroup," Mr Goni said.

The military spokesperson added that "military positions across Pulka remained securely under the control of the security forces."

He paid tribute to the members of the CJTF who "played an important supporting role during the operation by providing useful local information and assisting the troops in maintaining situational awareness."

Mr Goni said troops further carried out an "operation" to determine extent of battle damage, recover abandoned weapons, and obtain intelligence that could help track down fleeing terrorists.

The military spokesperson said the coordinated response "demonstrated the effectiveness of joint efforts in confronting terrorist threats across the theatre."

"Troops remain firmly deployed and on heightened alert across the area, with aggressive patrols, surveillance and other offensive and defensive operations continuing to deny terrorist elements freedom of movement and action," he said. "The military will sustain pressure on the terrorists while taking necessary measures to safeguard the lives and property of law-abiding citizens."

items.title: Troops arrest suspected terrorist logistics suppliers, recover motorcycle spare parts in Yobe
items.summary: Troops of the Joint Task Force (North East), Operation HADIN KAI (OPHK), have arrested two suspected terrorist logistics suppliers and recovered a large quantity of motorcycle spare parts and other items allegedly intended for Boko Haram/ISWAP terrorists operating within the Yunusari-Mobbar general area. Captain Mohammed Goni, Acting Military Information Officer, Joint Task Force (North East), […]
items.body: Troops of the Joint Task Force (North East), Operation HADIN KAI (OPHK), have arrested two suspected terrorist logistics suppliers and recovered a large quantity of motorcycle spare parts and other items allegedly intended for Boko Haram/ISWAP terrorists operating within the Yunusari-Mobbar general area. Captain Mohammed Goni, Acting Military Information Officer, Joint Task Force (North East), disclosed this in a statement on Wednesday morning, saying the operation was conducted on Tuesday, September 8, 2026, following credible human intelligence on the movement of logistics supplies suspected to be destined for terrorist elements. “Acting swiftly on the intelligence, troops of 159 Battalion under Sector 2 OPHK, in conjunction with other security elements, mobilised a fighting patrol and intercepted the suspected logistics consignment at Gumsa Bridge in Geidam Local Government Area of Yobe State,” the statement said. Items recovered during the operation include large quantities of motorcycle tyres, crankshafts, oil seals, traffic indicators, acceleration and clutch cables, bearings, brake components, gaskets, piston kits, chains and sprockets. Other recovered items include speedometers, clutch plates, rocker arms, CDI units, coils, rectifiers, fuel-related components and other motorcycle spare parts, 145 pairs of footwear and two Tecno Android phones, among others. The statement said the suspects and recovered items had been handed over to the 27 Military Intelligence Regiment for further investigation and necessary action. The successful interception represents another effort by the troops to disrupt terrorist logistics networks and deny terrorists critical supplies required to sustain their activities. The Joint Task Force (North East), OPHK, said it remained committed to dismantling terrorist support networks across the North-East Theatre. The statement advised members of the public to continue providing credible and timely information to security agencies to support ongoing counter-terrorism operations. items.title: Interrogating Defence Minister’s Declaration of Victory over Terrorists, Bandits
items.summary: A new chapter may be unfolding in Nigeria’s fight against terrorism and banditry as Minister of Defence, General Christopher Musa’s declaration of victory signals growing confidence, renewed hope, and a
items.body: A new chapter may be unfolding in Nigeria’s fight against terrorism and banditry as Minister of Defence, General Christopher Musa’s declaration of victory signals growing confidence, renewed hope, and a potentially decisive turning point in the nation’s security efforts, writes Linus Aleke . The declaration by the Minister of Defence, General Christopher Musa (rtd), that Nigeria has achieved victory over terrorists and bandits deserves to be examined not merely as a political statement, but against the operational realities and measurable gains recorded by the Nigerian security forces. Interestingly, this is not the first time the Federal Government has declared victory over the rampaging and bloodthirsty violent extremists operating in the country. In December 2015, the late President Muhammadu Buhari declared that Boko Haram had been “technically defeated”, following major territorial gains by Nigerian forces against the insurgents. In an interview with the BBC on 24 December 2015, Buhari said technically, the Nigerian military had won the war against Boko Haram, explaining that the insurgents could no longer mount conventional attacks against security forces or population centres and had been restricted largely to the use of improvised Explosive Devices (IEDs). The declaration followed a major military campaign that had recovered territories previously held by the insurgents. Contemporary reports therefore presented Buhari’s assessment as a claim of technical victory rather than an assertion that every Boko Haram fighter or attack had ceased. Still in December 2015, the then Minister of Information and Culture, Alhaji Lai Mohammed, similarly declared that the Federal Government had “largely won” the war against Boko Haram. Speaking after leading a team of 33 local and international journalists to areas at the centre of the insurgency in Borno State, including Maiduguri, Konduga, Kaoure and Bama, Mohammed said: “Today, I can report that the war against Boko Haram is largely won.” He explained that he could make the declaration based on what he had personally witnessed during the tour, adding that the entire 70-plus-kilometre stretch from Maiduguri to Bama and onwards to Banki was in the hands of Nigerian troops. He further stated that the terrorists had been so degraded that they could no longer hold territory or carry out spectacular attacks. Four years later, on 21 October 2019, Mohammed reaffirmed the position during a working visit to the corporate headquarters of a newspaper house in Lagos. Asked about his earlier assessment of the insurgency, he stood by it unequivocally, saying: “I stand by what I said that Boko Haram is technically defeated.” Mohammed explained, however, that Nigeria was then confronting a broader form of global terrorism involving groups and networks such as ISIS, ISWAP and Al-Qaeda. Fast-forward to Thursday, September 3, 2026, and barely 11 years after the previous administration declared technical victory over violent extremists, Minister of Defence, General Christopher Musa (rtd.), reiterated the Federal Government’s claim of victory in the ongoing fight against insurgency and other forms of violent extremism. Musa said attacks by terrorists and extremist groups were no longer as rampant or brazen as they had been in the past. Speaking during an interview on a national television programme, monitored by THISDAY, he observed that terrorist attacks had drastically reduced, giving way largely to kidnappings. Asked whether Nigeria had defeated terrorists or merely displaced them, Musa said: “Frankly speaking, we have defeated terrorists because now, like I said, the attacks are not as rampant and it is now kidnapping.” He said security had improved under President Bola Tinubu, adding that reports of terrorist attacks were no longer as frequent as they once were. According to him, “I can tell you there is improved security. May be if you noticed, you don’t hear so much of Boko Haram attacks, ISWAP attacks and all these things here and there, maybe one-off.” Musa argued that the security situation was following a downward trajectory from criminality to kidnapping, terrorism and insurgency, noting that once security forces successfully hit such groups, they were forced down the scale of operations. He added that kidnappings had become an easier means for criminals to raise funds. The Minister also stressed that troops were now entering terrorists’ enclaves and recovering many abducted persons. Musa’s position appears to be supported, at least in part, by recent operational figures released by the Defence Headquarters in August 2026. Director of Defence Media Operations, Major General Michael Onoja, reported that Nigerian troops had killed more than 324 terrorists and criminals and apprehended 373 others in August, 2026 alone. Onoja said the August figures reflected a marked improvement in operational effectiveness, driven by intensified kinetic and non-kinetic operations, enhanced intelligence, inter-agency cooperation and increased pressure on criminal and terrorist networks. More significantly, surrendered terrorists rose from 11 in June to 57 in July and 201 in August, suggesting increasing pressure on hostile elements and a possible willingness among some fighters to abandon terrorism. Civilian rescues also increased substantially in August, while arms and ammunition recoveries rebounded. These figures provide important context for Musa’s declaration. Yet acknowledging these gains does not require ignoring the continuing threat. The 2026 Global Terrorism Index reported that terrorism-related deaths in Nigeria increased from 513 in 2024 to 750 in 2025, representing a 46 per cent rise. Nigeria consequently ranked fourth globally in terrorism-related deaths. These figures suggest that victory should be understood as an ongoing process rather than the complete disappearance of every violent group. Indeed, this distinction may strengthen rather than weaken Musa’s position. A military can achieve strategic superiority while still confronting residual insurgent cells, criminal gangs and isolated attacks. The critical question is whether these groups are becoming increasingly incapable of challenging the authority of the state. Security experts, however, remain divided. Veteran Defence Correspondent, Madu Onuora questioned the basis of the declaration, asking: “victory over which terrorists?” He described the Minister’s declaration as premature and at variance with the reality on the ground, drawing parallels with previous declarations of victory, including Buhari’s 2015 “technical defeat” claim, former Chief of Army Staff, Lt. Gen. Tukur Buratai’s 2018 assertion that absolute victory was “inches away”, and his 2020 declaration that the military had “won the ground war”. According to Onuora, the situation remains complex. While the capabilities of terrorists may be degraded, he argued that the infrastructure sustaining terrorism remains largely intact. He said efforts should therefore focus on dismantling deeply entrenched terror networks while addressing the root causes of radicalisation and the governance failures that breed and sustain recruitment. Similarly, Chairman of the Guild of Public Affairs Analysts of Nigeria, Enugu State Chapter, Dr Ambrose Igboke, cautioned against confusing military effort with the complete resolution of insecurity. “While we need to encourage our military personnel and urge them to do more, we cannot begin to dance around the subject matter of continued insecurity in our country,” he said. According to Igboke, terrorists cannot be described as defeated while they retain the capacity to carry out large-scale attacks and inflict significant casualties. He urged the government to avoid turning the issue into political propaganda. A more measured assessment came from the Head of the Department of Political Science at Benue State University, Makurdi, Prof. Atah Pine, who acknowledged that the Nigerian Armed Forces had recorded encouraging successes against rural banditry and terrorism in recent times. “They have won several battles, no doubt, but the war is not over,” he said. “To declare defeat over banditry and terrorism at this point is not in sync with the reality of the situation. It is like putting the cart before the horse.” Former Ministry of Foreign Affairs spokesperson, Ambassador Ogbole Amedu-Ode, offered a more sympathetic interpretation of Musa’s position. He said it was gratifying to hear such a declaration from a retired general who had “paid his dues in and out of the trenches”, adding that he was inclined to believe Musa because of his antecedents. Nevertheless, Amedu-Ode said the real measure of victory would be felt when terrorism and those who profit from it had been defeated to the point where farmers could safely return to their fields and secure the nation’s food supply chain. This is perhaps the most important test of the declaration. Properly understood, Mu

items.title: 2027: I’ll stop crude theft, guarantee adequate supply to refineries — Adebayo
items.summary: The Social Democratic Party (SDP) presidential candidate, Adewole Adebayo, has pledged to halt crude oil theft and ensure adequate feedstock for Nigeria’s refineries if elected president in the 2027 election. The post 2027: I’ll stop crude theft, guarantee adequate supply to refineries — Adebayo appeared first on The Sun Nigeria .
items.body: The Social Democratic Party (SDP) presidential candidate, Adewole Adebayo, has pledged to halt crude oil theft and ensure adequate feedstock for Nigeria’s refineries if elected president in the 2027 election. Adebayo said tackling crude theft would be central to his administration’s strategy to strengthen domestic refining, improve energy security, and reduce poverty without imposing additional financial burdens on Nigerians. The SDP candidate made the remarks while speaking in an interview on ARISE NEWS, where he outlined some of the economic policies contained in his presidential blueprint. Adebayo said Nigeria could significantly improve crude availability for domestic refineries by ending the diversion of crude oil and strengthening monitoring of production and transportation. “If I stop associating with thieves, stop doing business with them, and stop stealing the crude—which we can easily monitor with Gulf of Guinea—you can’t steal the crude,” he said. According to him, Nigeria had previously set aside substantial crude volumes to support domestic refining as part of efforts to reduce poverty and improve the availability of petroleum products. He said the volume originally earmarked for domestic refining was about 450,000 barrels per day, adding that increasing domestic refining capacity would reduce Nigeria’s dependence on imported petroleum products. Adebayo argued that the country could guarantee sufficient crude supplies to its refineries without necessarily increasing government expenditure if crude theft was effectively eliminated. “That alone, without any additional expenditure, I will be able to guarantee you adequate supply,” he said. The SDP candidate also maintained that government must play an active role in strategic sectors of the economy rather than completely withdrawing from commercial activities. He said Nigeria’s mixed-economy model justified government investment in areas such as energy, agriculture, aviation and manufacturing, particularly where such investments could create employment and strengthen essential services. “Our Constitution says we will run a mixed economy, and I’m not shy about government jobs. After all, why should I deny a Nigerian a government job? The job I’m asking for—the presidency—is a government job,” Adebayo said. He also proposed large-scale investment in renewable energy, including a plan to install between 11 and 15 kilowatts of solar capacity on every roof within 11 months of assuming office. Adebayo said the initiative would not only improve electricity access but also create employment through the local production and installation of solar equipment. He projected that the proposed solar clusters could generate as much as 32,000 megawatts, while the national grid would serve primarily as a backup system. The SDP candidate said his approach would be to use government spending to address multiple challenges simultaneously, arguing that expenditure on sectors such as education and electricity could also translate into job creation. He said, “I’m thinking that the money I spend on education is also going to employment, because teachers are going to earn salaries.” Adebayo’s proposals form part of his broader 2027 campaign agenda, which focuses on strategic government investment, domestic production, employment generation and reducing Nigeria’s dependence on imported goods and services. The post 2027: I’ll stop crude theft, guarantee adequate supply to refineries — Adebayo appeared first on The Sun Nigeria .

items.title: Gridlock As Kara Bridge Repairs Take Toll On Lagos-Ibadan Expressway
items.summary: The two-week rehabilitation project, directed by the Minister of Works, Senator David Umahi, involves the replacement of deteriorating expansion joints to improve road safety, structural integrity, and long-term traffic flow on the busy corridor. The post Gridlock As Kara Bridge Repairs Take Toll On Lagos-Ibadan Expressway appeared first on Channels Television .
items.body: The two-week repair work on the Kara bridge is beginning to take its toll on free movement of vehicles on the Lagos-Ibadan expressway axis, as motorists remain stranded for several hours on Tuesday and Wednesday morning. The Federal Government announced the commencement of work on the damaged expansion joints of the bridge, beginning on Tuesday, September 8, 2026, a move that has triggered a massive gridlock, according to our correspondents who monitored the situation. The project, earlier slated to commence in August 2026, was suspended for traffic review following public outcry over short notice and the need for effective traffic management. However, commencement of the exercise has triggered massive traffic along the corridor since Tuesday, stretching from the Kara Bridge in Ogun State to the 7Up Junction in Lagos State, and beyond. While motorists plying the road, as of 4:00 PM on Tuesday, witnessed an extension even beyond the Secretariat Bus Stop, those coming from Ikeja and Agege to access the Otedola underpass were also locked in the tight vehicular procession, which stretched beyond the Otunba Jobi Fele Way. As of Tuesday afternoon, joint security officials were seen alternating between vehicles heading towards Kara from Isheri and Ojodu, with those coming from the expressway, in an attempt to prevent a total lockdown. The heavy presence of the police and military, alongside officials of the Lagos State Traffic Management Authority, Federal Road Safety Corps, and Ogun State Traffic Compliance and Enforcement Corps, could not placate the situation, as the repair work further worsened traffic at the bridge’s entry and exit points inward OPIC, around the Kara Bridge. As of Wednesday morning, as early as 5:30 in the morning, motorists were seen plying one-way to get passengers to their destinations. Street urchins also took advantage of the situation as they scurried along the corridor in a chase after commercial drivers to earn quick money. Commuters have started lamenting the terrible situation of the exercise as many get stranded and are unable to meet up with appointments and early arrivals at their places of work. Speaking with our correspondent, a motorist, Tijani Akinyele, described the situation as “terrible”. According to him, motorists heading towards Mowe who had no viable alternative route on Tuesday have been forced to ply a one-way as of Wednesday morning. “We didn’t expect this whole repair would turn out like this. The situation is terrible, but there’s nothing I can do. “I will blame the government because they ought to have found a solution to this before now”, he said. Thompson, another motorist, appealed to the authorities to find a lasting solution to the traffic situation. “We can’t continue like this. If the situation is like this today, what will it look like for the next two weeks?”, he lamented. The spokesperson for the Ogun State Traffic Compliance and Enforcement Agency, Babatunde Akinbiyi, urged motorists to exercise patience and cooperate with traffic officials during the repair period. Akinbiyi said the agency had anticipated the possibility of gridlock and had consequently issued a traffic advisory ahead of the commencement of the repairs. He said, “We anticipated that there would be traffic, and that was why we issued a traffic advisory earlier. “We can only appeal to motorists to bear with us for the time being because the repair works are necessary to ensure smooth movement and the safety of road users along the corridor. “Anyone who does not have an important business along the axis should stay away, and those who cannot avoid using that route should cooperate with traffic officials.” A statement by the Lagos State Commissioner for Transportation, Oluwaseun Osiyemi, on Sunday, noted that the development is in line with the Federal Ministry of Works’ earlier announcement. The two-week rehabilitation project, directed by the Minister of Works, Senator David Umahi, involves the replacement of deteriorating expansion joints to improve road safety, structural integrity, and long-term traffic flow on the busy corridor. The project is expected to run through September 22, 2026. Lagos State Government advised motorists traversing the corridor to plan their journeys ahead. To minimise its impact on traffic, LASG explained that one half of the affected section will be closed at a time, while motorists share the other open half interchangeably. The government appealed to all motorists to exercise patience and cooperate with traffic managers to ensure the rehabilitation is completed in two weeks as scheduled. The post Gridlock As Kara Bridge Repairs Take Toll On Lagos-Ibadan Expressway appeared first on Channels Television .

items.title: Bank mourns as branch manager killed by kidnappers in Imo
items.summary: A Polaris Bank branch manager has been shot dead by suspected kidnappers in Owerri, Imo State. Two female FUTO students were also abducted. Read More: https://punchng.com/bank-mourns-as-branch-manager-killed-by-kidnappers-in-imo/
items.body:
A branch manager of Polaris Bank, identified as Mr Ossy, has been shot dead by suspected kidnappers after he reportedly resisted an attack within the premises of the Federal University of Technology, Owerri, Imo State. The incident occurred on Sunday evening while the banker, who was based in Owerri, was reportedly taking his children to the university. Two female students were also allegedly abducted by the fleeing gunmen during the incident. Sources said the late banker had gone to drop off his children, who are students of FUTO, when he was accosted by the gunmen. However, the bank, in a statement signed by the Head, Brand Management & Corporate Communication, Rasheed Bolarinwa, obtained by PUNCH Metro on Tuesday, said the deceased was reportedly taking his children to the university, when he was attacked by hoodlums. The bank said the children managed to escape from the scene, but the manager was not as fortunate. “We are deeply saddened by the tragic death of our Branch Manager and extend our heartfelt condolences to his family, friends, colleagues, and loved ones during this difficult time. “The unfortunate incident occurred on Sunday, when he was accosted by the hoodlums, and while the children managed to escape from the scene, he was not that lucky. “We understand that the matter is being investigated by the relevant law enforcement agencies, and we trust that the circumstances surrounding the incident will be thoroughly established. “Our thoughts and prayers remain with the family of the deceased, and we respectfully urge the public to allow the authorities to complete their investigations,” the bank stated. Meanwhile, the management of FUTO confirmed that a visitor was fatally shot within the university campus during the incident. In a statement signed by the Registrar, Chinonso Uba, the institution stated that two female students were also abducted. The statement read, “The management of the Federal University of Technology, Owerri is deeply saddened by the tragic security incident that occurred on the university campus on Sunday, September 6, 2026, during which a visitor to the university was fatally shot. Fund family planning to fight insecurity in West Africa, gynaecologists tell govts Crisis as Federal Girls College management, PTA clash 2027: SDP Adebayo challenges Tinubu, vows to defeat insecurity “Two female students were also reportedly abducted during the incident. The circumstances are currently under investigation by the relevant security agencies, and management is engaging with the appropriate authorities regarding the safe recovery of the students. “Management assures students, staff, parents and the entire university community that the safety and security of all members of the university community remain a top priority. Additional security measures are being implemented in collaboration with the relevant security agencies. “Members of the University community are urged to remain calm and vigilant, avoid unnecessary movement and promptly report any suspicious activity. “Further information will be provided as appropriate.” The incident prompted the FUTO management to meet with the Imo State Commissioner of Police, CP Audu Garba Bosso, on Monday over the rising security concerns around the university and its host communities. During the meeting, Bosso assured the university management of intensified security around the institution and neighbouring communities, particularly the Ihiagwa, Eziobodo, Obinze and Nekede axes. Meanwhile, a source who spoke on condition of anonymity said a proposed peaceful protest by some students over the killing had been cancelled following the university’s reaffirmation of its ban on unruly and rowdy gatherings after examinations. The FUTO Senate had, at its 495th and 501st meetings held on August 31, 2023, and April 29, 2024, respectively, banned all forms of senseless celebrations after examinations, citing wanton destruction of university property, particularly by graduating students. The university management also reaffirmed the prohibition at its seventh meeting held on Monday, September 7, 2026, warning students against activities capable of disturbing the peace of the institution and its host communities. The prohibited activities include rowdy behaviour, public revelry, disorderly conduct, littering, indiscriminate disposal of waste, blocking or obstructing roads and entrances, and damaging or defacing university property. The management also warned against any conduct that could threaten the safety and security of the university community. The police have yet to announce any arrest in connection with the killing and abduction as of the time of filing this report. Uche Okere

items.title: Military arrests two terrorist logistics suppliers in Yobe
items.summary: Troops of the Joint Task Force (North East), Operation Hadin Kai (OPHK) have arrested two suspected terrorist logistics suppliers and recovered a large quantity of motorcycle spare parts and other items allegedly intended for Boko Haram/ISWAP terrorists operating within the Yunusari-Mobbar general area. The post Military arrests two terrorist logistics suppliers in Yobe appeared first on The Sun N
items.body: Troops of the Joint Task Force (North East), Operation Hadin Kai (OPHK) have arrested two suspected terrorist logistics suppliers and recovered a large quantity of motorcycle spare parts and other items allegedly intended for Boko Haram/ISWAP terrorists operating within the Yunusari-Mobbar general area. Acting Military Information Officer, Headquarters Joint Task Force (North East), Operation Hadin Kai, Captain Mohammed Goni disclosed this in a statement issued on Tuesday. Goni said the operation was conducted on Tuesday following credible human intelligence on the movement of logistics supplies suspected to be destined for terrorist elements. “Acting swiftly on the intelligence, troops of 159 Battalion under Sector 2 OPHK, in conjunction with other security elements, mobilised a fighting patrol and intercepted the suspected logistics consignment at Gumsa Bridge in Geidam Local Government of Yobe State. “Items recovered during the operation include large quantities of motorcycle tyres, crankshafts, oil seals, traffic indicators, acceleration and clutch cables, bearings, brake components, gaskets, piston kits, chains and sprockets, speedometers, clutch plates, rocker arms, CDI units, coils, rectifiers, fuel-related components and other motorcycle spare parts. “Also recovered were 145 pairs of footwear, 2 Tecno Android phones amongst others,” the statement reads in part. The military spokesman said the suspects and recovered items have been handed over to 27 Military Intelligence Regiment for further investigation and necessary action. The statement further reads, “The successful interception represents another effort by troops to disrupt terrorist logistics networks and deny them critical supplies required to sustain their activities. “The Joint Task Force (North East) OPHK, remains committed to dismantling terrorist support networks across the North East Theatre. Members of the public are therefore encouraged to continue providing credible and timely information to security agencies to support ongoing counter-terrorism operations.” The post Military arrests two terrorist logistics suppliers in Yobe appeared first on The Sun Nigeria .

items.title: Dangote refinery: NMDPRA mulls legal battle over access restriction
items.summary: The Dangote refinery has secured a court injunction against the NMDPRA, sparking a legal battle over regulatory authority in Nigeria’s free trade zones. Read More: https://punchng.com/dangote-refinery-nmdpra-mulls-legal-battle-over-access-restriction/
items.body:
The Nigerian Midstream and Downstream Petroleum Regulatory Authority is weighing its next move to prevent it from losing regulatory authority over midstream and downstream companies located in free trade zones. Last week, a Federal High Court in Lagos issued an interim injunction restraining the NMDPRA from shutting down or interfering with the operations of the Dangote Petroleum Refinery in the Lekki Free Zone, Lagos. Justice Akintayo Aluko made the order while ruling on a motion ex parte marked FHC/L/CS/1174/26, filed and argued by counsel to Dangote Petroleum Refinery Nigeria Limited, led by Olawale Akoni and Abimbola Akeredolu. The refinery had approached the court following a letter dated August 24, 2026, in which the NMDPRA allegedly directed the suspension of the loading and truck-out of petroleum products from the refinery. In his ruling, Justice Aluko said he had carefully considered the application, the affidavit evidence, exhibits and submissions of counsel, including the NMDPRA’s letter. The judge noted that the refinery’s case was that the NMDPRA lacked regulatory or oversight powers over operations within free zones, including the Dangote Industrial Free Zone. Justice Aluko also referred to a letter dated March 2, 2026, issued by the Attorney-General of the Federation, which, according to the judge, stated that the NMDPRA was not entitled to exercise regulatory powers or oversight functions over operations within free zones. The judge further held that the refinery had satisfied the conditions required for the grant of an interim injunction. “Accordingly, I find merit in the application, and the same is hereby granted in terms of the reliefs sought,” Aluko ruled. When contacted, the spokesman of the NMDPRA, George Ene-Ita, declined further comments on the matter, saying, “I can’t comment on a case before the court.” While not denying the NMDPRA’s letter to shut the Dangote refinery, Ene-Ita refused to give details on why the regulator ordered the refinery to stop loading. However, other senior officials within the NMDPRA disclosed that the regulator is weighing the next move as far as the case and the ruling are concerned. It was gathered that the agency’s legal team and its management “will decide the next line of action”. In May, the NMDPRA declared that petroleum companies operating in free zones, export processing zones and other designated areas in Nigeria remain fully subject to the provisions of the Petroleum Industry Act 2021 and regulations issued under the law. The regulator stated this in an industry circular. Blackouts: Factories spend N1.3tn on alternative power NMDPRA rejects claims of unaccounted gas flare revenues Diesel races to N2,000, refiners seek govt rescue Free zones are designated areas created by the government to encourage investment and industrial activities through tax incentives, customs waivers and simplified business regulations. They include export processing zones, industrial parks and special economic zones where companies often enjoy exemptions from certain taxes and administrative procedures. However, the NMDPRA stressed that such incentives do not exempt oil and gas operators from petroleum sector regulations under the PIA. “The operation of any midstream or downstream petroleum facility within a free zone, export processing zone or similar area does not exempt such facility and its operations from compliance with the provisions of the PIA and regulations made thereunder,” it stated. In the circular addressed to managing directors and chief executives of oil and gas midstream companies, downstream firms, petrochemical and fertiliser companies, as well as import and export terminals, the authority reaffirmed its statutory powers over all midstream and downstream petroleum activities nationwide. It explained that the regulatory mandate of the agency extends to all midstream and downstream petroleum activities and applies throughout Nigeria, including the continental shelf, territorial waters, exclusive economic zone, free zones, export processing zones, industrial zones and any other designated areas. The agency said it was the statutory regulator responsible for the technical, commercial, operational and licensing regulation of all midstream and downstream petroleum operations in Nigeria. It informed operators that all midstream and downstream petroleum operations, including refining, processing, storage, bulk transportation, pipelines, gas transportation networks, terminals, jetties, wholesale supply, importation, exportation, distribution and the sale of natural gas and petroleum liquids, are subject to its regulatory oversight. With the current ruling, the NMDPRA is expected to defend its authority over free zones while the court decides whether or not it has such powers. In its application, the Dangote refinery has asked the court to restrain the regulator, its officers, agents, representatives, privies or any person acting under its authority from enforcing or implementing the directive to shut the facility pending the hearing and determination of its motion on notice. The company also sought an interim injunction restraining the NMDPRA and its agents from entering, sealing, shutting down, restricting access to, obstructing, suspending, disrupting, inspecting, supervising, sanctioning or otherwise interfering with its refinery, petrochemical, terminal, storage, blending, loading, truck-out and related facilities and operations within the Lekki Free Zone. After granting the injunction, the court subsequently adjourned the case until September 9, 2026, for hearing of the motion on notice. Dare Olawin Dare Olawin is a journalist at Punch Newspapers with over a decade of reporting experience. He began his career as a community reporter and now covers the energy sector, including oil, gas, electricity, and renewables. Dare’s work reflects hands-on newsroom experience, professional development through workshops and conferences, and a strong commitment to accurate and insightful journalism.

items.title: 3 vigilantes killed in Kaduna
items.summary: Gunmen have killed three members of Kaduna State Vigilance Service (KADVIS) along the Zaria-Pambegua axis in Kubau Local Government Area. KADVIS spokesperson, Yunusa Shehu Ibrahim, said in a statement that the incident happened on Monday when the personnel were on routine security checks. He said the deceased attempted to stop a red Volkswagen Golf saloon […]
items.body: Gunmen have killed three members of Kaduna State Vigilance Service (KADVIS) along the Zaria-Pambegua axis in Kubau Local Government Area. KADVIS spokesperson, Yunusa Shehu Ibrahim, said in a statement that the incident happened on Monday when the personnel were on routine security checks. He said the deceased attempted to stop a red Volkswagen Golf saloon car, but the driver refused to stop, prompting the personnel to pursue the vehicle in an official patrol van to ascertain the occupants’ identity. He said the armed men subsequently opened fire on the personnel, killing the three personnel. Ibrahim identified the deceased vigilantes as Dallami Dantani, Abdullahi Hamisu and Zakariyya Musa. He added that the attackers later turned back towards the KADVS office, where they opened fire and fatally wounded Hamisu and Musa before fleeing towards Zaria. He also said hours after the attack, armed men abducted the younger brother of the Kaduna State House of Assembly member representing Kubau Constituency, Shehu Pambegua, at his residence in Pambegua, in the same LGA. He said the incident occurred at about 10pm on Monday when the suspected bandits, who reportedly arrived in a Sharon vehicle, invaded the lawmaker’s residence and whisked away his younger brother, identified as Sunusi. The Kaduna State Commander of KADVS, Ali Audu, expressed condolences to the families of the three personnel and described their deaths as a painful loss to the service and Kaduna State. He commended the deceased for their courage and dedication to duty, assuring their families that their sacrifices would not be forgotten. The commander assured that security personnel have heightened surveillance across Pambegua and surrounding areas, while efforts are ongoing to locate the victims and apprehend the perpetrators. He also urged personnel to remain vigilant and work closely with other security agencies to protect lives and property across the state.

items.title: 2027: Yayi reveals plan to appoint Ogogo as culture, tourism adviser
items.summary: The All Progressives Congress (APC) governorship candidate for the 2027 Ogun State election, Solomon Adeola, popularly known as Yayi, has revealed that he had planned to appoint the late veteran actor, Taiwo Hassan, popularly known as Ogogo, as his Special Adviser on Culture and Tourism. items.body: The All Progressives Congress (APC) governorship candidate for the 2027 Ogun State election, Solomon Adeola, popularly known as Yayi, has revealed that he had planned to appoint the late veteran actor, Taiwo Hassan, popularly known as Ogogo, as his Special Adviser on Culture and Tourism. Adeola, who currently represents Ogun West Senatorial District in the Senate, disclosed this on Tuesday when he visited Ogogo’s family at their country home in Ilaro, Ogun State. Speaking in a now viral video on social media, he said, “I planned to make Ogogo my Special Adviser on Culture and Tourism. Not just as SA but as a full cabinet member if I won the election and become the governor of Ogun State. “That was my plan. I kept it to myself and I was working with it. Believing that God will do it.” Ogogo died at 66 on August 23, 2026 after his battle with cancer. During the deceased battle with stage 4 cancer, Yayi was one of the primary financial backers, footing his medical bills. items.title: Obi urges FG to secure communities, return displaced Nigerians home
items.summary: Obi said he proceeded to Mangu after he and his delegation were prevented from reaching Yelwata, where they had planned to visit displaced Nigerians and families affected by recent attacks. The post Obi urges FG to secure communities, return displaced Nigerians home appeared first on Vanguard News .
items.body: The presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, has urged the Federal Government to intensify efforts to secure communities affected by attacks and facilitate the safe, dignified return of displaced Nigerians to their ancestral homes. Obi made the call in a statement posted on X on Wednesday after he visited an Internally Displaced Persons (IDP) camp in Mangu Local Government Area of Plateau State, following his inability to visit displaced persons in Yelwata, Benue State, on Tuesday. Obi said he proceeded to Mangu after he and his delegation were prevented from reaching Yelwata, where they had planned to visit displaced Nigerians and families affected by recent attacks. According to him, the situation in Mangu was “deeply disturbing,” with more than 45,000 people reportedly displaced and over 20 communities allegedly sacked by terrorists. “These are Nigerians who want nothing more than to return to their ancestral homes, rebuild their communities, cultivate their farms, and live their lives in peace and dignity,” Obi said. The former governor said he visited an IDP camp housing more than 500 displaced persons and offered support to the affected families as a gesture of solidarity. He stressed the need for the government to do more to protect communities affected by insecurity, arguing that the displacement of any Nigerian should concern the entire country. “As I have always maintained, as long as there is one displaced Nigerian, all Nigerians are displaced,” Obi said. He urged the government to protect the lives, safety, dignity and livelihoods of citizens regardless of their location, ethnicity, religion or political affiliation. “Our displaced citizens must not become forgotten Nigerians,” he said, stressing that the government must create the conditions for their safe return, secure their communities and support them in rebuilding their lives. Obi said the continuing displacement of Nigerians had disrupted homes, livelihoods and the future of affected communities, adding that the situation required urgent and sustained government intervention. He said his visit to the Plateau camp was also intended to draw attention to the plight of displaced citizens who, according to him, should not be left to fend for themselves. “The New Nigeria we seek must be a country where every citizen can live, work, farm, raise a family and pursue their dreams in peace and security,” Obi said. The visit came a day after Obi and his team were reportedly stopped from proceeding to Yelwata in Benue State to visit an IDP camp following recent attacks in the area. items.title: 'Earn the Trust of Kenyans', Dig Lagat's Message to GSU Recruits
items.summary: [Capital FM] Nairobi -- Newly trained General Service Unit officers have been urged to combine firmness in dealing with security threats with respect for the rights and dignity of the people they will be called upon to serve.
items.body:
Nairobi — Newly trained General Service Unit officers have been urged to combine firmness in dealing with security threats with respect for the rights and dignity of the people they will be called upon to serve.

Deputy Inspector General of the Kenya Police Service Eliud Lagat said effective policing requires more than courage in confronting danger, insisting that officers must also demonstrate restraint, sound judgment and humanity.

Lagat was speaking on Tuesday at the National Police College Embakasi "B" Campus during a full-dress parade rehearsal for Recruits' Detail 1B/2025.

The DIG told the recruits that their transition from training to active service would expose them to difficult people, complex situations and moments when their decisions would have far-reaching consequences.

"Be courageous, but remain professional. Be firm, but humane," he said.

Lagat reminded the recruits that some of their most important tests would come when they are operating without direct supervision.

He said an officer's discipline must therefore be internalised rather than dependent on the presence of a senior officer.

The DIG said the ultimate measure of the recruits' success would be their ability to earn and maintain the confidence of the Kenyan public.

He noted that protecting the public is at the heart of policing and urged the recruits to understand that the authority vested in them comes with an equally important responsibility to respect those they serve.

Lagat described the rigorous GSU training as preparation for the demands of security work, saying the programme was designed to push recruits beyond their comfort zones and build the character required of officers entrusted with national security.

The former GSU Commandant also encouraged the recruits to take pride in their new identity and wear the GSU badge with honour and courage.

He commended their instructors for their dedication and commitment throughout the training programme, urging the recruits to remain disciplined and focused as they prepare to join the service.

Lagat concluded by challenging the officers to uphold the reputation of the Kenya Police Service and, above all, serve in a manner that makes the people of Kenya proud.

items.title: Benue and Obi
items.summary: The presidential candidate of the National Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, was on Tuesday prevented by some youths from proceeding to Yelwata community in Guma Local Government Area of Benue State to commiserate with victims of deadly attacks by armed invaders. This is the second time the presidential candidate would be prevented from entering Benue, […]
items.body: T he presidential candidate of the National Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, was on Tuesday prevented by some youths from proceeding to Yelwata community in Guma Local Government Area of Benue State to commiserate with victims of deadly attacks by armed invaders. This is the second time the presidential candidate would be prevented from entering Benue, after his planned visit to internally displaced persons’ camps in the state was stopped in April, 2025. It was learnt that Obi and his entourage arrived in Makurdi, the state capital, on Tuesday morning but were reportedly stopped by the youths who blocked his convoy along the Gboko road, near the Nigerian Air Force Base. Witnesses said the former governor of Anambra State’s convoy was halted by the stick-wielding youth along the road while he was trying to get into Makurdi town after landing at the airport. Firm to equip entrepreneur’ trainers with ILO programmes Mother, son remain in captivity 3 weeks after abduction A witness, Denen Terkaa, said some of the young men threw stones at the convoy while others spread across the roads to hinder Obi’s movement. Speaking to our correspondent on the telephone in Makurdi, the Benue South Zonal Chairman of the NDC, Abu Suleiman, who was part of Obi’s entourage, confirmed the development. He said, “I was in the entourage. The youths barricaded the road from the airport axis. He (Obi) opted to talk to them, but they refused. After waiting for over an hour, he turned back and flew to Jos (Plateau State).” He described the development as “worrisome and barbaric.” He said: “I can’t just understand why they won’t let Obi visit the suffering villagers who have suffered several attacks by armed invaders. This is the second time he would be prevented from entering Benue.” Also, a resident of Makurdi, Adoor John, claimed that he had got wind of an emergency meeting held by some youths on Monday night to mobilise their counterparts from across the 23 local government areas of the state. John alleged that the meeting might have connections with the visit of the NDC presidential candidate. A group of youths blocking the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) presidential candidate, Peter Obi and his team from entering Benue State yesterday. Reason for the blockade unknown – Police The Police Public Relations Officer (PPRO) in the state, DSP Orchia Peter Aondongu, said operatives provided security for Obi and the command was aware of the incident. He, however, said the reason the convoy was blocked by some youths “is still unknown.” “We are monitoring the situation and investigating the circumstances surrounding the incident. Further updates will be provided accordingly,” the PPRO added. The state Commissioner of Police, Cletus Nwadiogbu, while addressing journalists later on Tuesday at the command’s headquarters in Makurdi, also confirmed that youths barricaded the roads because they did not want to see a particular high-profile individual. The CP said, “Yesterday night (Monday), we got information that His Excellency, former Governor of Anambra State, Peter Obi, will be coming, not for campaign but just to visit Yelwata. I said okay, everybody has freedom of movement in Nigeria. So I provided security. “I also asked the Assistant Commissioner (AC) Operation to personally lead the men, but unfortunately, on his arrival, we heard that the youths blocked the road because they didn’t want to see him. We are going to find out why the youths behaved that way. “We have tactically managed the situation for now, but we are not letting it go. We must get to the bottom [of the matter] to know why the youths said somebody cannot move. He (Obi) is a very responsible man. He saw that the youths blocked the road and I learned he went back and left.” Our correspondent reports that Obi had, about two weeks ago, visited Otukpo-Nobi area of the state following an attack on the community where 18 people were killed in June by invaders. The condolence visit had reportedly attracted a large crowd of supporters, during which Obi sympathised with the affected villagers and donated relief materials. Recall that in April 2025, Governor Hyacinth Alia, in a statement released by his Chief Press Secretary, Tersoo Kula, banned unapproved visits by prominent personalities to the state. The ban came on the heels of Obi’s planned visit to the state to tour some IDPs’ camps. The governor had explained that he was involved in critical high-level meetings with key stakeholders to address pressing issues affecting the state and cautioned against groups or prominent individuals entering the state without prior clearance, especially where such visits could lead to politically charged gatherings. “For anyone considering a visit to Benue State without the knowledge or approval of the governor, it is important to reconsider, as their safety and security cannot be assured,” the statement read. Obi looking for our trouble, says Benue govt The state Commissioner for Information and Orientation, Chief Solomon Iorpev, said the former Anambra governor should have formally notified the state government of his planned visit to guarantee his safety. “A high-profile person who has been a former governor of a state is coming into the state. He should have written a letter to the state government. We are supposed to guarantee his safety and protection, but where no letter was written, we could not guarantee his safety. “This is not the first time he has done this. He is just looking for our trouble. We are peace-loving and hospitable people,” he said. The commissioner explained that there was supposed to be a meeting of youths from the 23 LGAs of the state, saying, “if they were coming from either Tarka, Gboko, Buruku, Ushongo, Konshisha or Vandeikya at the same time of his visit and blocked the road, it is unfortunate. I do not know the youths who did that.” Benue State Commissioner for Information, Solomon Iorpev ‘Rascality totally unacceptable’ Obi, who addressed his supporters before departing to Jos after the obstruction, said he was not in Benue to campaign, but to condole with villagers affected by attacks. He said, “I’m in the state to visit where people have been killed. Over 200 people lost their lives. So I decided to come and condole with them and now youths led by a Special Adviser (SA) to the Governor have decided to block the road and make sure that I don’t go there. “I have been standing here for a while now, thinking they would come to their senses, but it is not happening. We cannot have a country like this. It doesn’t make sense to me. The rascality they are bringing into this country is totally unacceptable. We must have a country where people can live in peace and security. “People are being killed every day in Benue. People want to show their solidarity and comfort. People want to condole with them. People want to show that they are with them. I came here all the way this morning, a long distance from here, only to be told what you are seeing here. We cannot build a nation like this. “I am calling on Nigerians that they must come out and decide how we can build this country. This country belongs to all of us. These youths that are being used to do this, what they are doing now will take its revenge on them. They don’t know this. “And unfortunately, somebody sits in the office and allows this to happen. I have been a governor. Go and ask anybody in Anambra State; this wouldn’t have happened. We don’t need this. These people are hungry. These people are insecure. These are people that we need to pull out of poverty by giving them the opportunity of a livelihood, and that is one of the reasons why I came here. Unfortunately, you can see what is happening.” The NDC presidential candidate, however, promised to return to Benue if the need arises. Also, the governorship candidate of the party in Benue State, Prof. Terhemba Shija, who was with Obi, condemned the incident and commended Obi for his calm disposition. Shija said Obi’s handling of the situation showed he was ready to take the country forward, lamenting that peace had eluded several parts of Benue State for a long time. He recalled that when Obi contested for the presidency in 2023, he was marginally defeated by about 2,000 votes “despite rigging.” “At that time, many of us were not with him. Most of the politicians in Benue State have now seen the light. We have teamed up behind Peter Obi. There is no way a group in the minority is going to defeat us. Now that we have seen how they want to approach it, we want to assure them that we are ready for them. “We are going to launch our campaign in a week’s time, and nobody will stop us. This is our state. This state has suffered a lot. The government has normalised this suffering. Over one million people are in IDP camps. “There are a lot of ungoverned spaces in this state. In many places you go in Benue, there are no schools, no markets and no social activities. You can’t go to Gum

items.title: Jetour Rely R8 sets for Abuja debut
items.summary: Jetour Nigeria is set to introduce the highly anticipated RELY R8 premium heavy-duty pickup truck to motorists and automotive enthusiasts in Abuja as the company takes its flagship showcase, The Jetour Experience, to the Federal Capital Territory from September 22 to 24, 2026. The Abuja event follows the strong reception recorded during the Lagos showcase […]
items.body: Jetour Nigeria is set to introduce the highly anticipated RELY R8 premium heavy-duty pickup truck to motorists and automotive enthusiasts in Abuja as the company takes its flagship showcase, The Jetour Experience, to the Federal Capital Territory from September 22 to 24, 2026. The Abuja event follows the strong reception recorded during the Lagos showcase and is expected to attract government officials, corporate executives, fleet operators, business owners, automobile enthusiasts and members of the media. The major attraction of the three-day event will be the all-new RELY R8, a premium pickup designed to combine heavy-duty capability with the comfort, technology and refinement traditionally associated with luxury sport utility vehicles. Jetour Nigeria said the event would provide prospective customers and automotive stakeholders with an opportunity to experience the R8 first-hand, including through test drives. Positioned as a versatile workhorse, the RELY R8 is designed for demanding sectors such as agriculture, construction, logistics and security. The vehicle is engineered to operate in challenging conditions while providing occupants with a refined driving experience. Its off-road capability is enhanced by high ground clearance, a reinforced chassis and an All-Terrain Management System featuring dedicated modes for mud, sand and asphalt. According to the company, the combination makes the pickup suitable for demanding work environments as well as recreational and adventure activities. The R8’s interior is designed around a spacious five-seat configuration, with SUV-inspired ergonomics aimed at providing comfort during long-distance journeys and demanding work schedules. The pickup also features a smart cockpit powered by a high-performance processor and equipped to support Level 2+ intelligent driving assistance. Other technology features include a 12.3-inch HD touchscreen, Apple CarPlay, Android Auto and remote engine-start functionality. Jetour Nigeria is also placing emphasis on after-sales support and ownership confidence, backed by its network of seven accredited dealerships across the country. The dealerships include Elizade Nigeria Limited, New Era AutoVehicle Services, Kojo Motors, Germaine Auto Centre, Tab Autos, R.T. Briscoe Motors and Mandilas Motors. Customers will have access to manufacturer warranty protection, genuine spare parts and authorised service facilities as part of the company’s ownership support. Jetour’s growing presence in the Nigerian automotive market has also earned industry recognition. The automaker was recently named Fastest Growing Auto Brand of the Year by the Nigeria Auto Journalists Association (NAJA), while its Jetour Dashing was recognised as Car of the Year at the NAJA International Auto Awards. With interest expected from commercial operators, corporate executives and premium fleet customers, Jetour Nigeria is inviting prospective owners and automobile enthusiasts to attend the Abuja showcase and experience the RELY R8. The company said the event would offer visitors an opportunity to explore the pickup’s combination of rugged performance, advanced technology and executive comfort.
