items.title: Nigeria to migrate from consumer to producer of technology – NITDA
items.summary: The Director-General and Chief Executive Officer of the National Information Technology Development Agency (NITDA), Mr Kashifu Abdullahi, said Nigeria’s digital transformation must go beyond technology adoption to fundamentally change how the country creates value and improves productivity. He stated this at a pre-summit virtual dialogue on Tuesday ahead of the 32nd Nigerian Economic Summit (NES#3
items.body: The Director-General and Chief Executive Officer of the National Information Technology Development Agency (NITDA), Mr Kashifu Abdullahi, said Nigeria’s digital transformation must go beyond technology adoption to fundamentally change how the country creates value and improves productivity. He stated this at a pre-summit virtual dialogue on Tuesday ahead of the 32nd Nigerian Economic Summit (NES#32), “Digital Nigeria: The Foundation for Transformation,” organised by the Nigerian Economic Summit and the Federal Ministry of Budget and Economic Planning He described digital self-determination as the capacity to make meaningful choices about Nigeria’s digital future and stressed the importance of building, adopting and deploying technologies that advance national prosperity and security. He identified digital literacy and talent development as critical foundations, highlighting ongoing efforts to integrate digital skills into formal education, equip civil servants and strengthen technology talent pipelines. Abdullahi also emphasised the importance of enabling policies, digital infrastructure and access to markets in unlocking Nigeria’s technology potential. “With Nigeria’s young population, entrepreneurial energy, large domestic market and growing technology ecosystem, we have the potential to move from being primarily a consumer of technology to becoming a producer, builder and exporter of digital capabilities,” he said. He called for greater investment in local talent, infrastructure, companies, platforms, research and algorithms, while ensuring that data is transformed into economic value within the country. Co-Founder of TradePal AI, Mr. Femi Adegolu, called for a simpler and more coordinated regulatory environment to support innovation and participation in Nigeria’s digital economy. While noting the significant growth of the country’s fintech ecosystem, with more than 400 fintech startups, he identified regulatory fragmentation, operational friction and trust as key constraints. He advocated a harmonised licensing pathway across the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) and the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN), alongside tiered capital requirements that would enable smaller startups to enter the regulated ecosystem and incentives for data residency that would encourage the retention of Nigerian data and its economic value within the country. Speaking on enterprise readiness for digital transformation, Mrs. Adedoyin Odunfa, Founder and CEO of Digital Jewels Limited, said organisations must focus on the business value of technology rather than technology adoption for its own sake. She stressed the importance of establishing a clear business case before investing in technology, including defining the problem to be solved, the opportunity to be captured, the organisation’s capacity to deliver and the associated risks. She also called for technology platforms to have appropriate controls embedded from the outset, alongside stronger organisational capabilities in cybersecurity, risk management, compliance and artificial intelligence. Ms. Ojoma Ochai, Managing Director of Co-Creation Hub (CcHUB) Africa, noted that the success of innovators and startups depends on a functioning ecosystem rather than any single intervention. Representing the National Commissioner/Chief Executive Officer of the Nigeria Data Protection Commission (NDPC), Dr. Vincent Olatunji, Ibukunoluwa Owa highlighted the Commission’s efforts to promote innovation while strengthening data protection compliance. She referenced the Commission’s 2020–2027 Roadmap and Action Plan and its experience working with innovators through an informal regulatory sandbox to help them understand and meet data protection requirements.

items.title: At CIBN Conference, FG Challenges Banks to Do More for Economy
items.summary: • Cardoso: No economy can thrive with weak banks, says reforms soon to yield tangible benefits • Apex bank tightens scrutiny of banks over terrorism financing •World Bank: Banks must
items.body: • Cardoso: No economy can thrive with weak banks, says reforms soon to yield tangible benefits • Apex bank tightens scrutiny of banks over terrorism financing •World Bank: Banks must redirect capital towards job-creating sectors, reduce reliance on govt securities for yields • Dele Alabi: True test of reforms is lowering living costs, more jobs, higher real incomes, affordable credit, reduced poverty, commends CBN for macroeconomic stability • Economic management team moves to harmonise key macroeconomic assumptions Ndubuisi Francis, James Emejo in Abuja and Nume Ekeghe in Lagos President Bola Tinubu yesterday challenged Nigerian banks to move beyond balance-sheet expansion and profitability by deploying more capital to productive businesses capable of driving investment, job creation, and economic growth. Tinubu spoke at the opening of the 19th Annual Banking and Finance Conference of the Chartered Institute of Bankers of Nigeria (CIBN) in Abuja. The conference had the theme, “Building a Resilient Economy in an Era of Disruptions: Strategic Imperatives for the Banking and Financial Services Industry.” Tinubu declared that the banking industry must shift from financial intermediation to economic transformation. Represented by Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Mr. Taiwo Oyedele, the president said the country’s improving macroeconomic stability should not be mistaken for prosperity, stressing that the ultimate objective of the ongoing reforms is to translate stability into investment, production, jobs, and improved living standards. Governor of Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN), Mr. Olayemi Cardoso, said the country’s economic recovery could not be sustained without a strong and high-performing banking sector. Cardoso, who spoke at the CIBN conference, acknowledged the sacrifices made by banks and other stakeholders during the reform process, saying the reforms would soon yield concrete benefits. CBN stepped up its focus on terrorism financing risks across the financial sector, making it a supervisory priority as it moves to strengthen safeguards against the misuse of the financial system. That was as the Economic Management Team (EMT), the federal government’s principal platform for economic management and coordination, approved the establishment of a dedicated inter-agency committee to harmonise the macroeconomic assumptions underpinning government’s budgeting and economic planning. At the CIBN event, also, World Bank Country Director for Nigeria, Mr. Mathew Verghis, challenged banks to redirect capital from government securities towards businesses capable of creating jobs. Verghis warned that the current structure of bank profitability could come under pressure as interest rates declined. President/Chairman of Council of CIBN, Dr. Dele Alabi, said the ultimate test of economic reforms would be whether improved macroeconomic indicators translated into tangible improvements in the lives of citizens. Tinubu told the audience at the conference, “A resilient banking system cannot exist indefinitely where businesses cannot obtain affordable credit. Manufacturing that is struggling cannot expand, and millions of productive companies remain outside the formal financial system.” He said the current phase of the country’s reform journey was accelerating the conversion of stability into investment, investment into production, production into jobs, and growth into improved living standards. Tinubu said the banking and financial services industry was central to the current transformation process. “Therefore, we need to move from intermediation to transformation,” he stated. The president explained, “For years, we have measured financial institutions by balance sheet growth, profitability, and shareholder returns. These remain important, but we must increasingly ask: what is the financial system doing for the real economy? “A resilient banking system cannot exist indefinitely where businesses cannot obtain affordable credit. “Manufacturing that is struggling cannot expand, and millions of productive companies remain outside the formal financial system.” Tinubu urged banks to reassess how they allocated capital, stressing that the success of the recently concluded banking recapitalisation exercise should be measured by its impact on the real economy rather than merely by larger balance sheets. “A bigger bank that does not finance a more productive economy is a suboptimal outcome,” he said. The president said the federal government was strengthening guarantees, risk-sharing arrangements, blended finance and credit enhancement mechanisms, with the National Credit Guarantee Company at the centre of efforts to crowd private capital into productive investments. He explained that the government’s measure of success should increasingly shift from the volume of public spending to the amount of productive private capital it could catalyse. Tinubu identified growth facilitation, financial inclusion, technology, long-term capital, and trust as five imperatives for building a resilient financial system. On inclusion, he said access to a bank account was not enough, stating that genuine financial inclusion should enable small businesses to obtain affordable working capital while allowing young entrepreneurs to borrow based on viable cash flows rather than collateral they might not possess. The president called for greater deployment of patient capital to infrastructure, industry, housing, and energy, stressing that long-term development cannot be financed predominantly with short-term funds. He said the government’s reforms were already producing stronger macroeconomic indicators, citing 4.43 per cent real GDP growth in the second quarter of 2026, headline inflation of 15.43 per cent, and foreign reserves of more than $54 billion. Tinubu also pointed to Nigeria’s removal from the Financial Action Task Force grey list, its exit from European Union’s AML/CFT deficiency list, the planned reclassification of the country by FTSE Russell as a Frontier Market, and improving investor confidence, as evidence of progress. However, he cautioned that the gains represented the foundation rather than the final objective. Tinubu said, “Stability is the foundation; prosperity is the destination,” adding that the next phase of reforms must accelerate the conversion of “stability into investment, investment into production, production into jobs, and growth into improved living standards”. The president urged banks to move away from excessive reliance on government securities, which he said had made lending to productive businesses comparatively less attractive. He envisaged a cycle in which stronger fiscal discipline would reduce government borrowing pressure; lower inflation; support lower interest rates and affordable capital; stimulate investment and production; and generate jobs, incomes, and tax revenues. Tinubu also challenged banks to see Nigerian businesses as potential regional champions, particularly with access to the African Continental Free Trade Area market of more than 1.4 billion people. He said the next chapter of Nigeria’s development should not merely produce larger financial institutions but “a bigger and more productive economy where capital reaches and gets”. Cardoso: No Economy Can Thrive with Weak Banks Speaking at the conference, Cardoso said the country’s economic recovery could not be sustained without a strong and high-performing banking sector, while acknowledging the sacrifices made by banks and other stakeholders during the reform process. Represented by CBN Deputy Governor, Economic Policy Directorate, Mr. Philip Ikeazor, Cardoso said the macroeconomic stability achieved by the central bank was the product of unprecedented collaboration between the monetary and fiscal authorities. He credited Tinubu for granting CBN the independence to focus on its mandate, while commending the fiscal authorities, led by the Coordinating Minister of the Economy, for their cooperation. According to him, the major question now should be when ordinary Nigerians would begin to feel the full benefits of the reforms. “That is on its way,” he said, explaining that some of the fiscal reforms underway, alongside monetary policy measures, would soon begin to translate into tangible benefits. Cardoso said banks deserved recognition for their role in supporting the economy and for successfully completing the recapitalisation exercise. He said the exercise demonstrated both the depth of Nigeria’s domestic capital market and investors’ confidence in the economy. He disclosed that banks raised about N4.65 trillion from the domestic market. Cardoso stated, “Charity began at home. Our people put their money down — N4.65 trillion. So, when you see the confidence outside, it was also driven by that.” The CBN governor also acknowledged the cost of the monetary adjustment undertaken to contain inflation, saying the central bank has deployed substantial l

items.title: 2027 Elections: Benue Youths Stop Obi from Visiting Massacre Site in Yelewata
items.summary: • Presidential hopeful rebukes act, visits Plateau •We were not aware of his visit, Benue govt strongly dismisses alleged links with the thugs • We provided security, police declare •
items.body: • Presidential hopeful rebukes act, visits Plateau •We were not aware of his visit, Benue govt strongly dismisses alleged links with the thugs • We provided security, police declare • Kwankwaso, NDC, HURIWA, others decry devt Chuks Okocha, Onyebuchi Ezigbo, Sunday Aborisade, Alex Enumah in Abuja, George Okoh in Makurdi and Yemi Kosoko in Jos In what may be a foretaste of what lies ahead, as the 2027 election campaigns commence, the presidential candidate of Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Mr Peter Obi, was yesterday prevented by some Benue youths from visiting Yelewata community in Guma Local Government Area of the state, where he was scheduled to make personal donations to victims of the June 13, 2025 armed herdsmen attack. Obi, who arrived in Makurdi in the morning, was on his way to Yelewata when the youths blocked the Makurdi-Gboko Road less than two kilometres from the airport, chanting “Obi go back, Obi go back.” Some of the youths were reportedly wielding sticks and throwing stones as security personnel deployed to the area watched the development. Following the confrontation, Obi and members of his team turned back and returned to the airport, where he boarded his aircraft and left the state. Speaking before leaving, Obi described the development as ridiculous and very worrisome. He said he had travelled to Benue to sympathise with families affected by the killings and support victims of the Yelewata attack. Obi said, “It is ridiculous and very, very worrisome, our experience this morning. We arrived Benue, Makurdi precisely, this morning at 9am, on our way to the Yelewata community to condole and show solidarity to the families affected by last year’s killings. “As you know, there have been killings of over 270 persons in that community and I felt as we were starting our campaign that I should go around and be able to visit and condole the families, show respect to the dead and the community, support them in any way I can. “Only to arrive Makurdi this morning and trying to drive out, I was blocked by teaming thugs, shouting ‘Obi go back, Obi go back.’ And I was wondering, are we still in Nigeria? Or am I in another country? “But we know that even the campaigns have started, so I should be able to move around freely. But I discontinued because I didn’t want to say we must go on, as we have our own teaming crowd, but not wanting to cause confusion and possibly endanger the lives of other people. I decided to remain as civil as possible.” He appealed to the security agencies, particularly the Inspector-General of Police, Director-General of the Department of State Services, and other relevant authorities, to intervene and ensure that political campaigns were conducted peacefully across the country. Obi stated, “I am using this occasion to appeal to the security agencies, the Inspector-General of Police (IGP), the director of DSS, and other agencies to, please, intervene and be able to call various state governors to order. This rascality cannot be allowed. “We have a country and we, too, have followers. We have people who can confront these people on our own if the state and the government can no longer provide us security. We cannot go on this way. It is unacceptable.” He said the 2027 presidential campaign should be centred on issues affecting Nigerians, including insecurity, kidnapping, hunger, killings, and poverty, rather than violence and confrontation. He stated, “I participated yesterday in the commissioning of the office of the presidential candidate of APM, appealing that we need unity, love, justice, and let this campaign be concentrated on ideas, issues that concern Nigerians today – of insecurity, kidnapping, hunger, killing and everything and how we are going to pull our people out of poverty. That is what it should be. “I am not here to contest elections for office of the governor of Benue State. I have chosen as a presidential candidate that I want to visit every community, visit across Nigeria, which is what I’m urging other presidential candidates to do. “Go around Nigeria so you can feel the people, see their faces, ask them questions and they ask you questions about what you want to do for them, to be able to ameliorate the suffering Nigerians are going through today. That is why I am here today. Nothing else. “I call on the youths that are being used. The abuse you are allowing them to use you for today will take its revenge on you. I have a lesser number of years to live in life. “People are using you. They are not using their children. They are not using their relations. They are using you to stop opportunity of building a better life for you. “All I want is to have a Nigeria where a child of nobody can be somebody without knowing anybody. Where no Nigerian will go to bed without having food in his stomach, without knowing where the next meal will come from. That’s all we want.” The NDC presidential candidate said Benue had the agricultural capacity to feed Nigeria but lamented that insecurity and lack of economic opportunities had deprived many youths of sustainable livelihoods. He said, “Look at Benue, the state can feed Nigeria. It has arable lands where you can farm yam and lots of food crops. But today it has become a place where thugs thrive because they have no means of livelihood. And that is what we want to change.” Obi urged politicians and their supporters to avoid actions capable of plunging the country into anarchy, saying political contests should be determined by ideas and policies. He said, “We are not coming here fighting anybody because our elections will be run on ideas, on issues. And I urge people to, please, let’s concentrate on that. Let’s not allow a country to get into anarchy. Anarchy consumes everybody.” The former Anambra State governor said he found it difficult to believe that the incident could have occurred without the knowledge of the state government and security agencies. He said, “I have been governor myself. I know that this cannot happen without the government and security agencies in this state being fully aware that I am here. “I was governor for eight years and I know the system very well. And this couldn’t have happened while I was there. Even if it happens I will intervene.” Obi also stated that there was no justification for preventing him from moving around the state because campaigns had commenced. He said he was not visiting Benue on election day. According to him, “This is a campaign period. I did not come here on election day, so you cannot say I came disturbing the election. I did not come here when there was no campaign. “Remember last time I wanted to come, the governor said he did not want to see me. I turned back. But now is the election period where as a presidential candidate I am free to move around because elections campaigns have started. “So what they would have been doing is urging other presidential candidates to come and see things for themselves. I came to Benue to see things for myself.” The NDC governorship candidate in Benue State, Professor Terhemba Shija, who was at the scene, condemned the action of the youths and praised Obi for refusing to escalate the confrontation. Shija said Obi’s response demonstrated the kind of leadership he believed the former governor would provide if elected president. He stated, “You remember when Peter Obi contested for the presidency three or four years ago, in spite of all the rigging, he was marginally defeated by 2,000 votes. “Then a lot of us were not with him. items.title: Insecurity: Ex-Senator Gobir Backs Army Offensive, Vows No Sanctuary for Bandits
items.summary: Onuminya Innocent in Sokoto Former senator for Sokoto East, Abdullahi Gobir, declared full support for the ongoing military and security offensive against terrorists and bandits in Sokoto State, saying the
items.body: Onuminya Innocent in Sokoto Former senator for Sokoto East, Abdullahi Gobir, declared full support for the ongoing military and security offensive against terrorists and bandits in Sokoto State, saying the time has come to reclaim communities from criminal control. Gobir, also a member of the Niger Delta Development Commission (NDDC), said in a statement that the persistent attacks on rural areas constituted an unacceptable assault on human lives, agriculture, and the socio-economic fabric of the state. According to him, the escalating insecurity in Sokoto East and other vulnerable parts of the state could no longer be tolerated, and must be met with sustained, coordinated, and intelligence-driven operations by security agencies. He stated, “The people of Sokoto have endured enough. Terrorists and bandits must not be allowed to dictate the future of our communities or hold innocent citizens hostage through fear and violence.” Gobir commended the Nigerian Army, Nigeria Police, Department of State Services (DSS), Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC), and the Community Guards Corps for intensifying operations aimed at flushing criminal elements out of their strongholds. Gobir stated that the recent deployment of additional personnel and heavy military equipment to flashpoints was evidence of renewed determination by authorities to retake territories where terrorists had operated with increasing audacity.

items.title: At Interfaith Prayer, Sanwo-Olu Vows to Campaign for Tinubu Across 36 States, FCT
items.summary: • Hamzat seeks violence-free election as Obanikoro urges APC unity Wale Igbintade Lagos State Governor, Mr. Babajide Sanwo-Olu, yesterday, at an interfaith prayer session, pledged to take the campaign for
items.body: • Hamzat seeks violence-free election as Obanikoro urges APC unity Wale Igbintade Lagos State Governor, Mr. Babajide Sanwo-Olu, yesterday, at an interfaith prayer session, pledged to take the campaign for President Bola Tinubu’s re-election beyond Lagos, promising to make himself available to campaign for the president across the 36 states of the federation and the Federal Capital Territory (FCT). The interfaith prayer session was organised by All Progressives Congress (APC), with Christian, Muslim and traditional religious leaders offering prayers for the victory of the party’s candidates and a peaceful electoral process. The gathering marked a spiritual launch of the APC mobilisation for the 2027 elections. Party leaders called for unity, divine guidance, and victory for APC candidates at both the national and state levels. Sanwo-Olu said he would actively participate in the campaign for Tinubu’s re-election, stressing that the president’s victory is important to both Lagos State and Nigeria. He said he would make himself available to participate in the presidential campaign for the president and other party candidates. The governor stated, “I will make myself available to ensure that I go on the presidential campaign for Mr. President and all of us that are in that. That is what the wish of Lagos is. That is what the wish of Nigeria is. And that is what the wish of God is.” Sanwo-Olu said he would remain committed to the presidential campaign throughout the electioneering period, stressing that it should not receive less attention. He said the prayer session was designed to commit APC’s campaign and electoral activities to God, adding that the party is not taking voters, stakeholders, or the forthcoming elections for granted. The governor also expressed confidence in APC’s prospects in Lagos, particularly the candidacy of his deputy, Dr. Obafemi Hamzat, who is seeking to succeed him as governor. He said the party would work across the state to secure victory for Hamzat and its candidates for the National Assembly and state House of Assembly. Sanwo-Olu said by the grace of God and with the support of party members and Lagosians, God Almighty would make it possible for Hamzat to be elected governor. He stressed that prayers must be matched with hard work, urging party members to complement their faith with effective mobilisation. In his remarks, Hamzat acknowledged the prayers offered by the different religious groups, stating that Christian, Muslim and traditional leaders have all sought divine intervention ahead of the elections. He thanked those who attended, saying the Christian leaders have prayed and the Lord has answered their prayers, while the Muslim faithful prayed and Almighty Allah has answered. He added that the traditional leaders had also prayed and expressed the hope that God would answer those prayers. Hamzat said the gathering was convened to place Nigeria, Lagos State, APC, its leaders and candidates in the hands of God ahead of the elections. He prayed for Tinubu, First Lady, Senator Oluremi Tinubu, Sanwo-Olu, and his wife, Dr Ibijoke Sanwo-Olu, as well as other APC candidates. Hamzat specifically prayed for a violence-free electoral process, saying no party member or voter should lose his or her life during the elections. Director-General of the Hamzat Campaign Organisation, Musilu Obanikoro, urged APC members to close ranks and approach the 2027 election as one political family. Speaking on the theme, “Let God Go Before Us,” Obanikoro said strategy, organisation, hard work and commitment were essential to electoral success, but prayer also had a role to play in political affairs. He warned against allowing internal disagreements to undermine the party’s prospects following its primaries. He said internal contests must not be allowed to destroy the larger cause, adding that the primary has been concluded months earlier and everyone should close ranks. He stated that there should be no room for bitterness, division, recrimination, or working at cross-purposes. Obanikoro said opposition parties would confront APC as a single political entity regardless of differences among its members. He said the party’s opponents would not distinguish between one aspirant and another but would confront APC as a political party. He added that if the opposition viewed APC as one, the party must respond as one. He urged party members to campaign with respect and avoid allowing political disagreements to degenerate into personal conflicts. He said the party members had competed with dignity and should campaign with respect, disagree without becoming enemies and stand together for the collective interest of the party. Obanikoro expressed confidence in APC’s candidates at the national and state levels, describing them as people with proven integrity. He urged party members to combine prayer with unity, discipline, and hard work as the 2027 campaign gathered momentum.

items.title: Domestic crisis: Violence tearing Lagos homes apart
items.summary: RECENTLY, the kitchen is no longer the only place getting hot in Lagos homes; every room is on fire. Marriage is supposed to be about partnership, but in 2026, for a growing number of Lagos couples, it’s about who throws the first punch. She threw the plate. He threw the first punch. The post Domestic crisis: Violence tearing Lagos homes apart appeared first on Vanguard News .
items.body: By Olasunkanmi Akoni RECENTLY, the kitchen is no longer the only place getting hot in Lagos homes; every room is on fire. Marriage is supposed to be about partnership, but in 2026, for a growing number of Lagos couples, it’s about who throws the first punch. She threw the plate. He threw the first punch. By morning, the marriage of five years had two black eyes and a broken dining table. Meanwhile, Lagos has handled approximately 700 cases involving male victims of domestic abuse over the past one year. It also recorded 33,009 cases between late 2021 and mid-2026, perhaps highlighting an intensified legal crackdown despite heavy caseloads. DSVA Executive Secretary, Titilola Vivour-Adeniyi, disclosed this when she led a delegation on a courtesy visit to Vanguard Media’s Apapa office. She fingered economic pressure, mental health strain, and a culture of silence as top culprits, turning domestic disputes into full-blown fights. In 2026, “till death do us part” is taking on a more literal meaning for too many couples, she said. Across apartments in Alimosho, Surulere, Ikorodu, and Lekki, arguments over money, stress, and infidelity are no longer ending in slammed doors. They are ending in fisticuffs. Husbands and wives, once partners, are now throwing punches. And as violence tears Lagos homes apart, what used to be whispered as “marital issues” is now spilling into hospitals, police stations, and the streets. Beyond Physical Violence Domestic and sexual violence extends far beyond physical violence to include emotional, verbal, and financial abuse. From arguments over school fees to late nights and WhatsApp messages, violence has moved from the street into the bedroom. Counsellors, police, a n d survivors say the pattern is clear: Lagos homes are tearing apart, one fight at a time. The question is, what broke first: the home or the people in it? Women Bear Primary Brunt at 90%, as Reporting Revs Up According to Vivour-Adeniyi, the data released by the Lagos State Ministry of Justice and DSVA revealed over 711 cases formally charged to court. Approximately 88 per cent to 90 per cent of adult domestic violence reporters are female, though male victims account for about 10 per cent to 12 per cent of cases handled by the agency. Domestic violence, she said, accounted for the overwhelming majority of reported incidents, totaling 13,515 cases. Official demographic data showed that adult women continue to bear the primary brunt of abuse, representing approximately 90 per cent of reporting survivors, compared to roughly 10 per cent male reporters. The figure highlights a growing shift in public reporting as economic pressures continue to place a strain on household stability across the state. Lagos State Government, through the Domestic and Sexual Violence Agency, DSVA, has secured over 160 court convictions against perpetrators of Sexual and Gender-Based Violence, SGBV, in the last one year. Areas of Prevalence The local government areas (LGAs) consistently generating the highest number of reported spousal and adult domestic abuse cases, according to DSVA, include Alimosho, Ikorodu, Eti-Osa, Kosofe, Ikeja, and Oshodi-Isolo. Ikeja LGA Adopts Campaign Complementing the state government’s drive to curb the menace, the Ikeja Local Government has championed a sensitisation campaign and walk through the streets aimed at raising awareness and promoting peaceful homes across the council area. The exercise, which was held last Wednesday, was organised by the Women Affairs and Poverty Alleviation, WAPA, and led by council officials and community stakeholders. Participants displayed placards bearing various inscriptions, such as “Say No to Domestic Violence” and “Ikeja Says No to Domestic Violence,” as they called on the public to speak up against all forms of abuse. The exercise also focused on healthy communication, mutual respect, and peaceful conflict resolution, with residents urged to report cases of abuse while supporting victims and witnesses in accessing help promptly. Ikeja Local Government reaffirmed its commitment to building a community where residents can live free from violence, intimidation, and abuse. Homes in Crisis A recent case study happened in a Lagos suburb, while a quiet community in Ifo Local Government Area of Ogun State was left in shock after a Celestial Church pastor killed his wife during a domestic argument before later dying on the Lagos-Abeokuta Expressway. The incident happened in the early hours of Monday, August 31, at Ogooluwa community, Akiode Ibogun. The pastor, identified as Bidemi Odukoya, was the Shepherd of Iri Orun Parish of the Celestial Church of Christ, which he reportedly ran with his wife. According to accounts from residents, the couple had an argument around 2 a.m. Odukoya allegedly attacked his wife with a machete and a wooden stool, causing fatal injuries. After the attack, the father of three boys reportedly left the community and headed towards Coker Junction, along the Ifo section of the Lagos-Abeokuta Expressway. items.title: Abiodun: 100,000 Ogun Women Empowered to Fight Poverty, Strengthen Families
items.summary: James Sowole in Abeokuta Ogun State Governor Prince Dapo Abiodun has disclosed that about 100,000 women across the state have benefited from the World Bank-supported Nigeria for Women Programme (NFWP),
items.body: James Sowole in Abeokuta Ogun State Governor Prince Dapo Abiodun has disclosed that about 100,000 women across the state have benefited from the World Bank-supported Nigeria for Women Programme (NFWP), describing women’s economic empowerment as a strategic tool for fighting poverty and strengthening families and communities. Abiodun made the disclosure when he received the United Nations Deputy Secretary-General, Ms. Amina Mohammed, who joined him in interacting with beneficiaries of the programme at the Governor’s Office, Oke-Mosan, Abeokuta. The governor said his administration deliberately embraced and took ownership of the programme because it provided an opportunity to reach women at the grassroots who might otherwise remain outside conventional structures of political and economic empowerment. According to him, empowering women should go beyond appointing them to political offices to providing them with the resources, skills and opportunities required to build sustainable livelihoods, support their families and live with dignity. “When the World Bank shared with us the Nigeria for Women Project, we did not only key into it; we took ownership of it. “We saw in that programme the opportunity to empower women because not all women are able to contest elections or be appointed Commissioners or occupy political offices. We saw the opportunity to touch the lives of these women, empower them to support their households and themselves, and give them a sense of dignity,” he said. Abiodun said the programme’s impact had reinforced his administration’s conviction that investing in women was an investment in the wider economy and the future of families. He noted that economically empowered women were better positioned to provide for their households and contribute to community development. He said Ogun’s implementation of the programme had attracted delegations from more than 25 states seeking to study the state’s model, adding that political commitment remained critical to replicating its success. The governor expressed the hope that the initiative would be expanded across the country so that more women could benefit from the intervention. “It is my prayer that this deepens across the length and breadth of the 36 states and the FCT. I am filled with so much joy today that you are here and that you can see first-hand what we have been able to do with women empowerment,” Abiodun said. The UN deputy secretary-general commended the governor for providing seed funding for the programme and, more importantly, for believing in the capacity of women to grow their businesses and transform their communities. Mohammed praised the beneficiaries for demonstrating resilience, creativity and enterprise, saying their progress showed what could be achieved when women were given the right support and opportunities. “You have shown that you started small and you are growing, and what we want is for every woman in Ogun State who can benefit to have that benefit,” she said. The UN official said she would take the Ogun experience back to her home state and share it as an example of what could be achieved through deliberate investment in women. “I will take this initiative back to my state so that everyone will know that a seed was sown in Ogun State for the women of Nigeria, and that seed is growing. A country is as strong as its women,” Mohammed added. The State Coordinator of the Nigeria for Women Programme, Mrs. Bola Fadairo, disclosed that Ogun was among the first six pilot states when the programme was launched in 2020. She said the state had exceeded its target by 105 percent, with 8,759 Women Affinity Groups comprising 247,273 women established across the 20 local government areas. Fadairo added that beneficiaries had received training in financial management, record-keeping, gender awareness, life skills and other areas designed to equip them with the knowledge and skills required to build sustainable livelihoods. She said the scale of participation and the impact recorded across the state underscored Ogun’s commitment to creating sustainable opportunities for women to strengthen their livelihoods, improve household incomes and contribute meaningfully to the development of their communities.

items.title: Obi Blocked In Benue – A Warning Sign For The 2027 Campaign?
items.summary: The incident could reflect political hostility, a breakdown in local coordination, a security failure, or another cause. The post Obi Blocked In Benue – A Warning Sign For The 2027 Campaign? appeared first on Channels Television .
items.body: THE SIGNAL Peter Obi’s convoy was blocked by youths in Benue State on Tuesday while he was travelling along the Gboko, Makurdi road towards Yelwata, where he was expected to visit communities and families affected by recent violence. The police confirmed the obstruction and said security personnel were providing protection to the former Anambra State governor. The reason for the blockade, however, remained unclear. That distinction matters. Obi said youths, allegedly mobilised by a Special Assistant to the Benue State Government, were responsible. The Benue State Government denied any involvement and said it was not aware of the visit. So far, the incident establishes an obstruction. It does not establish who organised it or why. And that is precisely where the political significance begins. Videos circulating from the scene showed youths blocking the road as Obi’s convoy attempted to pass. Reports indicated chanting and confrontation around the convoy. The police confirmed that the convoy was stopped and said an investigation was underway. Obi described the visit as humanitarian rather than a campaign event, saying he was travelling to express condolences to communities affected by deadly attacks. Other opposition figures, including Rabiu Kwankwaso and Omoyele Sowore, condemned the obstruction. The Benue State Government, however, rejected suggestions that it organised the incident, saying it did not patronise thugs and expected proper coordination with security agencies over political visits. WHAT REMAINS UNRESOLVED Three questions remain central. Who mobilised the youths? Obi has made an allegation. The state government has denied it. That claim and denial cannot, by itself, establish responsibility. Why was the convoy blocked? The incident could reflect political hostility, a breakdown in local coordination, a security failure, or another cause. The available evidence does not yet allow a definitive conclusion. Could it happen again? That may ultimately be the more important question for the 2027 campaign. Nigeria is moving towards a much more intense political season. Candidates will increasingly travel into states and communities where political loyalties are contested and emotions are high. How those movements are managed will matter. WHY THIS MATTERS Elections are not only about who wins votes. They are also about whether candidates can compete for those votes under reasonably equal conditions. A candidate must be able to enter communities, meet voters and present a political argument without being physically obstructed. That does not mean every political visit will be welcomed. Protest, criticism and disagreement are part of democratic politics. But there is a significant difference between rejecting a candidate politically and preventing a candidate from reaching voters. The distinction becomes even more important when security arrangements fail to prevent a confrontation. THE WIDER OPPOSITION SIGNAL The incident comes as opposition politics is simultaneously showing signs of movement and uncertainty. On Monday, Obi appeared publicly with Oyo State Governor Seyi Makinde at the inauguration of Makinde’s APM presidential campaign office, where they unveiled a “Reset Nigeria” agenda. Obi has also indicated a willingness to work with any candidate who emerges through a free and fair process. That suggests that, despite continuing disagreements over who should lead an eventual opposition arrangement, engagement between key figures is continuing. The contradiction is notable: the opposition is still trying to create political space for cooperation at the national level, while individual politicians are already encountering the realities of campaigning on the ground. The immediate issue is not political speculation but the outcome of the police investigation. Watch for: •Whether anyone is identified as having organised the blockade. •Whether any arrests or charges follow. •Whether the Benue Government provides further evidence concerning its lack of involvement. •Whether Obi or other opposition candidates alter their campaign plans in response. •Whether similar incidents occur elsewhere as political activity intensifies. One incident does not establish a national pattern. But repeated incidents would begin to establish one. The evidence is incomplete. The standard is not: every candidate must be free to campaign safely and without obstruction. That is today’s Political Signal. It examines political developments, personalities and electoral trends without endorsement of any political party or candidate. Its assessments are based on publicly available evidence and may change as events and evidence develop. items.title: FG Sets Roadmap For Nationwide Rollout Of 112 Emergency Number
items.summary: The NEC had recently approved 112 as Nigeria’s single universal toll-free emergency number to replace fragmented and slow-response lines, with the aim of eliminating bureaucratic bottlenecks and giving citizens easier access to emergency assistance during fires, accidents, medical crises and security incidents. The post FG Sets Roadmap For Nationwide Rollout Of 112 Emergency Number appeared first
items.body: The Federal Government has directed relevant stakeholders and agencies to develop a comprehensive operational roadmap for the nationwide rollout of the 112 national emergency number. To this end, it has constituted a committee comprising the Nigeria Police Force (NPF), Nigerian Communications Commission (NCC), National Emergency Management Agency (NEMA), Federal Road Safety Corps (FRSC) and other relevant agencies to finalise the roadmap and standard operating procedures for formal endorsement by the National Economic Council (NEC). This was disclosed in a statement issued on Tuesday by the Senior Special Assistant to the President on Media and Communications, Office of the Vice President, Stanley Nkwocha. The NEC had recently approved 112 as Nigeria’s single universal toll-free emergency number to replace fragmented and slow-response lines, with the aim of eliminating bureaucratic bottlenecks and giving citizens easier access to emergency assistance during fires, accidents, medical crises and security incidents. Speaking in Abuja on Tuesday at the National Emergency Number 112 Project stakeholders’ meeting, Vice President Kashim Shettima directed the committee to ensure that its decisions and proposed framework were guided by global best practices. Shettima charged the committee to finalise the roadmap and standard operating procedures for formal endorsement by the NEC, stressing the need for the process to make significant progress. He also assured the stakeholders that resources would be made available to drive the implementation once the project becomes more visible. “Let’s make progress so that whatever time we have spent here is worth spending. And most importantly, the engine is finance. It is resources to drive the process. And I want to assure you that we will get the resources,” the Vice President was quoted as saying. The Inspector General of Police, Olatunji Rilwan Disu, expressed the Nigeria Police Force’s full support for the adoption of 112 as the country’s unified national emergency number. From an operational perspective, Disu described the initiative as “a significant step towards ensuring that citizens have a simple and reliable means of accessing emergency assistance.” He explained that citizens facing armed attacks, accidents, fire outbreaks, medical emergencies, kidnapping or other life-threatening situations often first have to determine which agency to contact, stressing that a single number should provide access to the appropriate response agency. Earlier, the Personal Assistant to the President on e-Governance, Office of the Vice President, Lydia Aina, said emergency response in Nigeria currently cuts across several agencies, systems and jurisdictions, resulting in fragmentation in how emergencies are received, coordinated and handled. She said the objective was to move from fragmented state-level systems to a coordinated response mechanism and ultimately establish a fully integrated national framework. According to her, the stakeholders’ meeting focused on the infrastructure and operational framework required to make the emergency number functional, including “the people, the agencies, the standards that make the number actually work when citizens dial it.” “Our job now is to turn it into an actual working programme with milestones. So, we have identified six immediate priorities. First, governance. We need a clear structure of who’s responsible for what,” she explained. Other stakeholders who pledged the full support of their agencies included the Director-General of NEMA, Zubaida Umar; Corps Marshal of the FRSC, Shehu Mohammed; and Director-General of the National Orientation Agency (NOA), Lanre Issa-Onilu, among others. items.title: Police intensify manhunt for two armed robbery suspects in Delta
items.summary: The two suspects attacked a 48-year-old man in his residence with a locally-made gun on Friday at about 5:30 p.m., the police said. The post Police intensify manhunt for two armed robbery suspects in Delta appeared first on Premium Times Nigeria .
items.body:
The Police Command in Delta State has intensified its manhunt for two armed robbery suspects in the state.

Bright Edafe, the police spokesperson in Delta, said in a statement on Tuesday in Warri that the suspects were among those terrorising Ekpan Community in Uvwie Local Government Area of the state.

He said the duo attacked a 48-year-old man in his residence with a locally-made gun on Friday at about 5:30 p.m.

Mr Edafe, a superintendent of police, said the incident was reported the same day at the Ekpan Division of the Nigeria Police.

The police spokesperson said the masked suspects broke into the victim’s house near Charlisco, on the NPA Express Road.

He said the victim courageously wrestled with the suspect holding the firearm, breaking the gun in the process.

Mr Edafe added that upon noticing this, the second suspect struck the victim on the forehead before both suspects fled, abandoning the broken firearm.

“Upon receipt of the report, the Divisional Police Officer, Ekpan Division, immediately deployed operatives to the scene, where the damaged locally-made firearm was recovered.

“The victim was referred to a hospital for treatment, while a manhunt for the fleeing suspects is in top gear,” he said.

Mr Edafe quoted the Commissioner of Police in the state, Samuel Erale, as commending the victim for his courage, and assured that the command would track and apprehend the suspects.

The police commissioner also solicited useful information from the public to assist the police in preventing crimes before they are committed in the state.

items.title: Drone strike near courthouse in North Kordofan kills 12
items.summary: A drone strike blamed on Sudan’s paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF) killed 12 people and The post Drone strike near courthouse in North Kordofan kills 12 appeared first on Radio Tamazuj .
items.body: A drone strike blamed on Sudan’s paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF) killed 12 people and wounded 20 others outside a courthouse in the army-held town of Um Rawaba in North Kordofan on Tuesday afternoon, army-aligned authorities and eyewitnesses told Radio Tamazuj. The strike was the latest in an escalating wave of drone attacks by the RSF and Sudanese army, which have been at war since April 2023. The drone struck an area outside the courthouse where residents had gathered to complete legal and administrative procedures, witnesses said. “The drone attack today targeted a courthouse in Um Rawaba and those killed are 12 and are all civilians, and many others have been wounded,” eyewitness Hamza Abdalla told Radio Tamazuj. The strikes sparked panic, prompting people to flee while others rushed to help the injured, the eyewitness said. Most of the wounded were taken to Um Rawaba Hospital for treatment, he added. Mohamed Salah, a spokesman for Sudan’s Emergency Lawyers Committee, a group of lawyers and human rights defenders, confirmed the reported toll of 12 dead and 20 wounded, including six lawyers and an employee of the judicial authority. “The attack targeted several areas, especially the courthouse, and those killed are 12 and wounded are 20 others,” Salah said. Salah said the attack occurred while legal professionals and court employees were carrying out their civilian duties. He described it as part of what he called a broader pattern of attacks on civilians and civilian infrastructure. The lawyers’ spokesperson said attacks on civilian and legal facilities violate international humanitarian law and warned that such incidents could disrupt judicial institutions and limit civilians’ access to justice. Salah said the attack followed previous strikes on civilian and legal facilities, including an attack on the Garra al-Zawiya court in North Kordofan in August. The North Kordofan state government condemned the attack in a statement obtained by Radio Tamazuj, describing it as an attack on civilian institutions and judicial facilities. حكومة شمال كردفان تدين استهداف المليشيا مجمع المحاكم بأم روابة https://t.co/0FDrcW2cOz #سونا #السودان pic.twitter.com/IqbpWOjt8T — SUDAN News Agency (SUNA) (@SUNA_AGENCY) September 8, 2026 An RSF military official declined to comment when reached by Radio Tamazuj, saying only that Um Rawaba was hosting a graduation ceremony at the time for a group of army-affiliated fighters. Um Rawaba lies along a strategic route linking central and western Sudan and has remained under army control despite repeated attacks in the surrounding region. Sudan’s war has killed more than 200,000 people, according to aid workers, displaced millions and created the world’s largest displacement and hunger crises. items.title: 2027: Security agencies strategise against election violence in Kogi
items.summary: Security agencies and electoral stakeholders in Kogi State have begun preparations for the 2027 general election, with officials calling for collaboration, compliance with electoral laws, and peaceful political campaigns. The post 2027: Security agencies strategise against election violence in Kogi appeared first on Premium Times Nigeria .
items.body:
Security agencies and other stakeholders in Kogi State have begun preparations for the 2027 general election, with a focus on preventing violence and other threats that could undermine the electoral process.

The stakeholders met in Lokoja under the Inter-Consultative Committee on Election Security (ICCES) to review emerging security threats and strengthen coordination ahead of the elections.

The Kogi Resident Electoral Commissioner, Shehu Wahab, who spoke at the meeting, said the committee had a responsibility to deploy its experience and resources to ensure voters could exercise their franchise peacefully.

He said the meeting provided an opportunity for security agencies to review security concerns and determine measures required to safeguard the electoral process.

The meeting, which lasted about two hours, was held behind closed doors as members reviewed security concerns and other issues surrounding the 2027 elections.

The Kogi State Commissioner of Police, Naziru Kankarofi, subsequently urged political actors to comply with electoral laws and avoid hate speech, incitement and other actions capable of disrupting public peace.

He also called for responsible political communication and peaceful campaigns ahead of the elections.

Mr Wahab said the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) was putting measures in place to support the work of ICCES and strengthen efforts towards a peaceful and credible election in the state.

He acknowledged that Kogi, like other states in Nigeria, has areas facing security challenges, adding that the security committee was designed to address such concerns through collaboration among relevant agencies.

The development comes a day after PREMIUM TIMES reported that Governor Ahmed Ododo banned night arrests and urged traditional rulers to work toward peaceful, violence-free elections.

Mr Ododo, while addressing first-class traditional rulers at the Government House in Lokoja on Monday, directed security agencies not to invade homes or make arrests at night.

He also urged the monarchs to discourage political thuggery, intimidation and violence, and to ensure that political campaigns are issue-based rather than driven by religion or ethnicity.

The governor’s directive and the latest security meeting come as Kogi begins early preparations for the 2027 electoral process, with stakeholders stressing the need for security agencies, political actors and communities to work together to prevent violence.

items.title: BCLCC : Le ministre Mahamadou Sana inaugure un studio dédié à la lutte contre les fakes news et à la sensibilisation à la cybercriminalité
items.summary: Le Ministre de la Sécurité, le Camarade Mahamadou SANA, a procédé, dans l’après-midi de ce mardi 8 septembre 2026, à l’inauguration du studio multimédia de la Brigade Centrale de Lutte contre la Cybercriminalité (BCLCC). Cette infrastructure moderne est destinée à renforcer la communication préventive et la sensibilisation des populations face aux défis croissants du numérique. … The post BCLCC :
items.body:
Le Ministre de la Sécurité, le Camarade Mahamadou SANA, a procédé, dans l’après-midi de ce mardi 8 septembre 2026, à l’inauguration du studio multimédia de la Brigade Centrale de Lutte contre la Cybercriminalité (BCLCC). Cette infrastructure moderne est destinée à renforcer la communication préventive et la sensibilisation des populations face aux défis croissants du numérique.

Doté d’équipements audiovisuels de dernière génération, ce studio servira à produire des capsules dédiées à la déconstruction des fausses informations (fake news), à la sensibilisation à la cybersécurité et à la vulgarisation de diverses thématiques en lien avec la sécurité.

À travers cet investissement, le Ministère de la Sécurité se dote d’un outil stratégique pour promouvoir une information fiable, développer une culture de cybersécurité et renforcer la résilience des citoyens face aux menaces numériques.

Le studio contribuera également à l’éducation des populations aux enjeux du numérique, à la prévention des risques liés à l’utilisation des technologies de l’information et de la communication, ainsi qu’à la promotion des bonnes pratiques en ligne.

Cette réalisation traduit la volonté du Gouvernement, sous l’impulsion du Camarade Président du Faso, le Capitaine Ibrahim TRAORE, de faire de la communication de proximité et de la prévention des risques numériques un levier majeur de la stratégie nationale de sécurité.

À travers des contenus pédagogiques, accessibles et adaptés aux réalités des citoyens, la BCLCC entend renforcer la vigilance collective et accompagner les populations dans une utilisation responsable et sécurisée des outils numériques.

items.title: RSF-aligned gov’t rejects UN fact-finding report as biased
items.summary: The paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF) aligned government, the Sudan Founding Alliance (Tasees) has rejected... The post RSF-aligned gov’t rejects UN fact-finding report as biased appeared first on Dabanga Radio TV Online .
items.body: The paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF) aligned government, the Sudan Founding Alliance (Tasees) has rejected a report by the UN fact-finding mission on Sudan, accusing it of bias and ignoring alleged crimes committed by the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF). The alliance said it remains ready to cooperate with international human rights mechanisms and reaffirmed its commitment to international human rights and international criminal law. The report , presented to the Human Rights Council on Monday, cited a cross-border network involving the UAE, Chad, Libya and Puntland that allegedly supports the RSF with weapons. It also referred to crimes committed in El Fasher. Tasees spokesperson Ahmed Tagad Lisan, said in a statement seen by Radio Dabanga that the report contained “fundamental systematic defects” that undermine its conclusions and legal credibility. He criticised the mission’s reliance on remote testimonies and interviews conducted away from the locations of alleged violations, saying investigators had failed to conduct direct field inspections. Tasees accuses report of ignoring SAF violations Tasees accused the report of systematically overlooking alleged violations by the SAF and allied militias, including the alleged use of internationally banned chemical weapons . Tagad Lisan said the report failed to provide a balanced assessment of responsibility. He pointed to alleged massacres in El Gezira state, Sennar, Suki, Singa and El Dinder, as well as the Haj Yousif, Mayo, El Salih and El Halfaya neighbourhoods of the capital following the SAF’s entry. He accused SAF forces and allied militias of carrying out “clean-up operations” involving the execution of hundreds of civilians, destruction of homes and farms, forced displacement and looting. Tasees said the omission of these alleged crimes raised questions about the report’s neutrality. Tasees accuses mission of bias Tasees also accused the report of presenting a one-sided account of foreign involvement in the war. It said the report highlighted alleged support for its forces from Chad, south-eastern Libya, Puntland, the UAE and Colombia, while failing to mention countries it said support the SAF, including Saudi Arabia, Egypt, Türkiye, Qatar, Iran, Algeria and Eritrea. Tasees also criticised the report for mentioning Colombian recruits fighting alongside its forces while allegedly omitting references to Eritrean military bases, Ethiopian forces, Egyptian forces and other foreign elements fighting alongside the SAF and allied militias. Tasees called for the report’s conclusions to be reviewed and for a direct field investigation under international supervision covering all conflict zones. It also called for investigators to hear from all parties and examine documented violations committed by all sides. items.title: Al-Burhan Meets ICGLR Delegation
items.summary: [SNA] President of Transitional Sovereignty Council (TSC) and Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces, General Abdel-Fattah Al-Burhan, met on Sunday with a delegation from the International Conference on the Great Lakes Region (ICGLR), headed by the organization's Secretary-General, Joël Kianda.
items.body:
President of Transitional Sovereignty Council (TSC) and Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces, General Abdel-Fattah Al-Burhan, met on Sunday with a delegation from the International Conference on the Great Lakes Region (ICGLR), headed by the organization's Secretary-General, Joël Kianda.

The meeting was attended by the Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation, Ambassador Mohi-Eddin Salem.

In a press statement, the ICGLR Secretary-General said the organization regarded Sudan as an important and pivotal country in Africa, describing the meeting with the TSC President as fruitful and constructive, particularly in light of Sudan's contribution to advancing African issues.

He stressed that Sudan believed in the need to resolve African problems within the African framework, away from international interference.

Kianda said the meeting also discussed a number of issues of mutual interest, foremost among them the importance of sustaining security and stability in the Great Lakes region and the wider region.

He said the ICGLR had confidence that the region was in safe hands and that Sudan was on the right path, reaffirming the organization's support for Sudan during the current critical phase until peace and stability are achieved throughout the country.

items.title: Finance Minister - Armed Forces Constitutional Institution Responsible for Protecting Sudan - Rejects Expansion of Arms Embargo
items.summary: [SNA] Chairman of the Sudanese Justice and Equality Movement (JEM) and Minister of Finance, Dr. Gebreil Ibrahim Mohamed, affirmed that the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) are the national institution constitutionally mandated to protect the country and defend its sovereignty and territorial integrity, announcing JEM's rejection of proposals to expand the arms embargo imposed on Darfur to cover all of
items.body:
Chairman of the Sudanese Justice and Equality Movement (JEM) and Minister of Finance, Dr. Gebreil Ibrahim Mohamed, affirmed that the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) are the national institution constitutionally mandated to protect the country and defend its sovereignty and territorial integrity, announcing JEM's rejection of proposals to expand the arms embargo imposed on Darfur to cover all of Sudan.

In a post on his official Facebook page following a meeting in Khartoum on Sunday with the UN Secretary-General's Special Envoy to Sudan, Pekka Haavisto, Dr. Gebreil said such a measure would undermine national sovereignty and restrict the Armed Forces' ability to fulfill their constitutional duty to protect the country.

The meeting discussed developments in Sudan, particularly the humanitarian situation and violations against civilians by the rebel Rapid Support Forces (RSF) militia.

Dr. Gebreil stressed the importance of the international community playing a supportive role in safeguarding Sudan's sovereignty, territorial integrity and the legitimacy of its national institutions.

He also reviewed prospects for the political process and pathways toward peace, stressing the importance of pursuing two complementary tracks simultaneously: the security track based on the Jeddah Declaration, and the political track through an inclusive Sudanese dialogue that excludes no one.

He called on the United Nations to welcome and support the Sudanese dialogue initiative and to work with Sudanese stakeholders to develop it into an inclusive, Sudanese-owned political process that would bring an end to the war and lay the foundations for sustainable peace and a stable state.

Dr. Gebreil reaffirmed the movement's commitment to integrating its forces into the Sudanese Armed Forces, stressing the importance of integrating all armed forces into a unified national army.

items.title: TSC President Meets UN Secretary-General's Special Envoy to Sudan
items.summary: [SNA] President of the Transitional Sovereignty Council (TSC) and Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces, General Abdel-Fattah Al-Burhan, met on Sunday at his office in the Republican Palace with the UN Secretary-General's Special Envoy to Sudan, Pekka Haavisto.
items.body:
President of the Transitional Sovereignty Council (TSC) and Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces, General Abdel-Fattah Al-Burhan, met on Sunday at his office in the Republican Palace with the UN Secretary-General's Special Envoy to Sudan, Pekka Haavisto.

The meeting discussed the overall situation in Sudan, efforts to strengthen security and stability, and the achievement of comprehensive peace in the country.

In a press statement, Haavisto said: "I conveyed important messages concerning de-escalation and the protection of civilians. We also look forward to continuing our meetings with a view to achieving the exchange of prisoners and civilian detainees, in close cooperation with the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC)."

Haavisto stressed that dialogue was the path to achieving sustainable peace and reaching a comprehensive ceasefire. He expressed his readiness to cooperate and engage in close dialogue with all Sudanese parties and stakeholders, and to work with partners in the Quintet to advance the political process and ensure that it is inclusive, comprehensive and responsive to the aspirations of the Sudanese people.

He also stressed the importance of holding unified examinations across the country, describing the issue as a major concern for the international community. The United Nations, he said, was working closely with UNICEF to safeguard children's fundamental right to sit for accredited examinations across Sudan.

Haavisto concluded his remarks by praising reconstruction efforts, saying: "I can see and observe many construction and reconstruction works bringing life back to normal in this city."

items.title: Nigeria: Clashes Claim 2 Lives in Bauchi
items.summary: [Daily Trust] The Bauchi State Police Command has arrested seven suspects in connection with the criminal conspiracy, inciting disturbance and culpable homicide that occurred in Dass Local Government Area on 4th September, 2026.
items.body:
The Bauchi State Police Command has arrested seven suspects in connection with the criminal conspiracy, inciting disturbance and culpable homicide that occurred in Dass Local Government Area on 4th September, 2026.

The command's Public Relations Officer, SP Nafiu Habib, who disclosed this in a statement, said preliminary investigation revealed that on the said date at about 1800hrs, one Ibrahim El-Safwan aka Jabala'i of Bayan Fada area, Dass, criminally conspired with his accomplices, intercepted and brutally attacked one Abdulrahman Nuru, 29-years-old, a tricycle rider of Bundot area, Dass, stabbing him with cutlasses on various parts of his body at Tudun Wus area, Dass.

Habib said that a team of policemen attached to Dass Division swiftly mobilised to the scene.

"On arrival, it was discovered that personnel of the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps, whose headquarters is close to the scene, had already taken custody of the tricycle and one suspect.

"The victim was immediately rushed to General Hospital, Dass, where he was subsequently confirmed dead by a medical doctor," he said.

Habib explained that the incident sparked tension in the area, as youths from Bundot area mobilised in large numbers, armed with cutlasses and other dangerous weapons, and stormed the Bayan Fada area for reprisal.

"This led to a violent confrontation between the two groups at an open space near Dass' Central Motor Park, during which another victim, Mukhtar Jibrin, 38 years old, of Bayan Fada area, was stabbed.

"Mukhtar was rushed to General Hospital, Dass, and later referred to the Abubakar Tafawa Balewa University Teaching Hospital, Bauchi, where he was also confirmed dead," he said.

He, however, noted that detectives swung into action, doused the tension, restored normalcy, and arrested the following suspects in connection with the ugly incident: Umar Abubakar 20-years-old of Bayan Fada area (principal suspect), Blus Garba 19-years-old Bundot area, Adamu Muhammad 17-years-old of Bundot area, Hussaini Danjuma 17-years-old of Bundot area, Hassan Danjuma 17-years-old of Bundot area, Shuaibu Sani 17-years-old of Bundot area, and Aliyu Abdullahi 18-years-old of Bundot area.

Habib further disclosed that relentless efforts are in top gear to apprehend other accomplices now at large.

items.title: Drought threatens Sudan’s agricultural season as food fears grow
items.summary: Farmers and residents across parts of South Kordofan and Darfur are warning that severe rainfall... The post Drought threatens Sudan’s agricultural season as food fears grow appeared first on Dabanga Radio TV Online .
items.body: Farmers and residents across parts of South Kordofan and Darfur are warning that severe rainfall shortages and prolonged dry spells are threatening this year’s agricultural season, raising fears of further food shortages and price rises. Residents in several areas of the Nuba Mountains told Radio Dabanga that rains have been scarce and interrupted, with unusually high temperatures damaging crops and threatening food security. In El Tadamon locality, residents said rainfall was below normal and insufficient for crops to continue growing, while the drought has extended across large areas. Residents of Abbasiya also warned that crops were increasingly vulnerable, raising fears of production losses, reduced food supplies and higher grain prices. A farmer in Abu Jubeiha told Radio Dabanga that drought had spread from the Habila and Liri agricultural projects through Abu Jubeiha, El Tadamon and Abbasiya, reaching areas south of Umm Rawaba. He said rains had stopped for more than 20 consecutive days amid severe and unusual heat . Some crops, particularly sorghum, sesame and peanuts, had been completely “burned” by the drought and could no longer be saved by later rainfall. Farmers have also reported unusually open roads between Abu Jubeiha and El Tadamon, and onwards to El Muqnas, Kosti, Talodi and Liri, allowing large trucks to move through areas where roads are normally disrupted during the autumn rains. The price of a sack of sorghum has risen from SDG70,000 to SDG120,000 amid the movement of crops from South Kordofan to El Obeid. No field surveys have yet been conducted in Abu Jubeiha by official, international or local organisations, making it difficult to estimate the scale of crop losses . Farmers said they had already lost money preparing land, buying inputs and paying labour, leaving them less able to prepare for the next season. Residents and farmers called for urgent field assessments, measures to restrict crop exports outside South Kordofan to protect local stocks, and immediate humanitarian intervention. ‘Darfur faces mounting drought’ Several areas of Darfur are also facing severe rainfall shortages, threatening agricultural production and raising concerns about food availability. In North Darfur, delayed and insufficient rains have left some farms dry while some farmers have yet to begin planting. Local emergency room members said villages west of Kutum and surrounding areas were facing a worsening crisis as delayed rains reduced pasture and water sources, threatening food security and livestock. It appealed for food, drinking water and support for water sources. In South Darfur, Adam El Fadil from Netika locality told Radio Dabanga that some farms had already reached the drought stage while others were waiting for rain before planting. He said cultivated millet had not yet reached half a metre, threatening basic crop production. He warned that food grain prices could rise to unaffordable levels. A sack of millet was selling for SDG280,000–300,000, while sorghum cost SDG220,000–230,000. Netika is among 13 South Darfur localities facing an emergency over rainfall shortages. In East Darfur, Hope and Refuge Organisations for Refugees and Support for Darfur Victims warned of rainfall shortages and agricultural failure in Abu Karinka. The group said rains had been interrupted for around three weeks, damaging large areas planted with millet and beans and forcing some farmers to use seed stocks, threatening next season’s planting. The organisation called on UN agencies, humanitarian organisations and donors to conduct an urgent assessment and provide food, seeds and agricultural inputs. ‘FAO warns of wider rainfall deficit’ The UN Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) reported that major agricultural areas in southeastern Sudan recorded significant rainfall deficits. Cumulative rainfall between June and mid-August was around 20 per cent below the long-term average in Sennar and 30 per cent below average in El Gedaref. FAO said severe moisture shortages had affected vegetation, with its Agricultural Stress Index showing severe drought across up to 40 per cent of cultivated land in Sennar and 70 per cent in El Gedaref. The agency warned that below-average rainfall during the June-September rainy season was already affecting germination and early crop development, while forecasts point to a high probability of below-average rainfall for the remainder of the planting season. Conflict has also disrupted farming in Darfur, Kordofan and Blue Nile, while insecurity , high input prices and limited access to credit continue to constrain agricultural production. FAO said sorghum prices rose by 65 per cent in most monitored markets between January and June, while millet prices increased by 42 per cent. Sudan’s 2025 cereal production stood at around 5.2 million tonnes, 22 per cent below 2024 levels and 19 per cent below the five-year average. The country is expected to need 2.8 million tonnes of cereal imports this year, mostly wheat, amid limited financial and logistical capacity. FAO estimates that 33.7 million people in Sudan will need assistance this year, including 19.5 million facing extreme hunger. Share article The post Drought threatens Sudan’s agricultural season as food fears grow appeared first on Dabanga Radio TV Online .

items.title: Man wanted over killing own family in UK pleads guilty to gun offenses in South Africa
items.summary: A man wanted by British police over the killings of his wife and two daughters pleaded guilty Tuesday to firearms offenses in South Africa, where he was arrested in July while on the run.
items.body:
A man wanted by British police over the killings of his wife and two daughters pleaded guilty Tuesday to firearms offenses in South Africa, where he was arrested in July while on the run.

Ndodana Mkhanyisi Tshuma's guilty pleas to charges of illegal possession of a firearm and illegal possession of ammunition were part of a plea deal, South African prosecutors said. Tshuma also pleaded guilty to an immigration offense for entering South Africa while he was a fugitive.

South African authorities say they will move to extradite him to the U.K. after his local court case is concluded. Prosecutors in the U.K. say he will be charged with three counts of murder.

Tshuma's wife, Nothabo Zandile Tshuma, and their daughters, Natalie, 15, and Nala, 5, were found dead at their home near the town of Bedford, north of London, on July 6. They had all suffered head injuries.

British police say they believe Ndodana Mkhanyisi Tshuma left the U.K. on July 4 and traveled to Zimbabwe and then arrived in South Africa before the bodies were discovered.

Tshuma, who was identified as a British citizen of Zimbabwean heritage, was arrested in Johannesburg on July 10 while in possession of a gun and ammunition after Interpol issued a notice for him to be apprehended.

South African police have said that they suspect he was going to use the gun to kill himself.

items.title: Guerre commerciale : Ottawa riposte aux États-Unis avec des contre-mesures sur 28 milliards de dollars
